findings.clause_text: Valeant shall have the right to review and approve (acting reasonably and in good faith) any such excess speaker programs, including with respect to the number of speakers approved to speak on the Product as part of the speaker programs, the rates paid to speakers at such speaker programs and the rules regarding attendees who may attend such speaker programs (including frequency of attendance)
findings.description: Valeant retains expansive approval rights over operational details of Dova's speaker programs, creating potential for operational interference, strategic misalignment, and commercial delays despite Dova being the product owner.
findings.reasoning: The scope of approval rights extends to granular operational decisions: specific speaker selection, compensation rates, and attendee management. In co-promotion agreements, the product owner (Dova) typically retains control over promotional strategy while the co-promoter (Valeant) executes detailing. Granting Valeant approval over speaker rates and selection inverts this hierarchy. The 'reasonable and good faith' standard is subjective and difficult to enforce, creating litigation risk if Dova disagrees with Valeant's rejection of key opinion leaders or commercially necessary speaker fees.
findings.remediation: Narrow approval rights to: (1) total budget caps for excess programs; (2) compliance with applicable laws and the Agreement; and (3) brand safety standards (removing Valeant approval over specific speakers, rates, and attendee rules). Replace 'approve' with 'consult' or 'right to provide input' for operational details. Add time limits for approval (deemed approved if not rejected within 5 business days) and specific objective standards for rejection (e.g., 'speaker has been debarred' or 'proposed rate exceeds industry standard by more than 20%').

findings.clause_text: If the Marketing Sub-Committee unanimously agrees that such excess speaker programs should be conducted, then the following costs and expenses will be shared equally by the Parties...
findings.description: Speaker program cost-sharing provision lacks corresponding allocation of liability, indemnification, or regulatory compliance responsibility for violations arising from these high-risk promotional activities.
findings.reasoning: Pharmaceutical speaker programs carry substantial regulatory exposure under the Anti-Kickback Statute, False Claims Act, and FDA promotional guidelines. While costs are shared 50/50, the clause is silent on: (1) who bears liability for regulatory fines or whistleblower actions; (2) indemnification for third-party claims; (3) responsibility for speaker compliance training; and (4) liability caps. Given Valeant's approval rights over program content, Valeant could argue it shares control and thus should share liability, but without explicit language, Dova as the program conductor faces primary exposure. The absence of a liability cap (e.g., limiting exposure to the amount invested in programs) creates unlimited downside risk for discrete promotional activities.
findings.remediation: Add comprehensive liability and indemnification provisions: (1) Each party indemnifies the other for regulatory violations or third-party claims arising from its own personnel's misconduct or breach of the Agreement; (2) Liability for speaker program-related claims is shared equally (50/50) consistent with cost sharing, unless caused by one party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (3) Cap each party's liability for speaker program claims at the total amount that party contributed to speaker programs in the calendar year in which the claim arises; (4) Specify that Dova, as program conductor, is responsible for day-to-day compliance monitoring, but Valeant shares liability for programs it approved.

findings.clause_text: The JSC shall consist of three (3) representatives from each Party... The meetings of the JSC will be chaired by a representative from Dova or Valeant, on an alternating basis.
findings.description: Equal representation on the JSC without a tie-breaking mechanism creates high risk of governance deadlock on operational decisions requiring JSC approval.
findings.reasoning: With three representatives from each party and no provision for tie-breaking (e.g., rotating casting vote, escalation to executives, or supermajority voting), any disagreement between the parties results in deadlock. This is particularly problematic given the JSC's oversight responsibilities over commercialization strategy, promotional materials, and dispute resolution (first-level escalation). The alternating chairperson provision confers no decision-making authority. Deadlock could paralyze critical business decisions, force premature termination, or require expensive arbitration for routine operational matters.
findings.remediation: Implement a tiered decision-making protocol: (1) For routine operational matters, decisions by majority vote of JSC members present, with the alternating chairperson having a casting vote in case of tie; (2) For strategic matters (e.g., brand plan changes, budget increases), escalate to designated executive officers (e.g., Chief Commercial Officers) for good faith negotiation; (3) If executive escalation fails within 14 days, either party may initiate formal dispute resolution (mediation/arbitration) or, for time-sensitive matters, the status quo prevails pending resolution. Alternatively, allocate decision rights by subject matter (e.g., Dova has final say on medical/scientific matters, Valeant on sales force deployment).

findings.clause_text: the additional incremental costs and expenses associated with training necessary to address the number of the speaker programs above and below the Speaker Program Threshold
findings.description: Ambiguous phrasing regarding training costs for programs 'above and below' the threshold creates risk of unintended cost-sharing for base-level training programs.
findings.reasoning: The clause intends to share costs of 'additional incremental' training necessitated by excess programs. However, the phrase 'training necessary to address the number of the speaker programs above and below' is grammatically ambiguous. It could be interpreted to mean: (1) training for both categories of programs (base and excess) is shared, or (2) the incremental training needed to handle the combined volume. Since base programs (below threshold) are presumably Dova's sole financial responsibility, sharing training costs for those programs would be an unfavorable and likely unintended result. This creates exposure for Dova to pay for Valeant's share of base training or disputes over cost allocation.
findings.remediation: Clarify the language to: 'the additional incremental costs and expenses associated with training necessary solely to support the speaker programs in excess of the Speaker Program Threshold, and not any training costs associated with speaker programs at or below the Speaker Program Threshold which shall be borne solely by Dova.'

findings.clause_text: The chairperson shall prepare and circulate for review and approval of the Parties minutes of each meeting within thirty (30) days after the meeting.
findings.description: Requirement for both parties' approval of JSC minutes creates risk of deadlock and disputes over the official record of decisions.
findings.reasoning: The provision requires approval by both parties (implied by 'approval of the Parties'), meaning either party can block approval. This creates risk that one party prevents formalization of minutes to dispute the record of decisions later, particularly if the minutes reflect decisions that party now regrets or disagrees with. Without a 'deemed approved' mechanism or dispute resolution, minutes can remain in limbo indefinitely, creating uncertainty about what was actually decided and evidentiary problems in future disputes.
findings.remediation: Add deemed approval language: 'Minutes shall be deemed approved unless a Party objects in writing within 10 business days of circulation, specifying the disputed portions. Undisputed portions shall be approved immediately. Disputed portions shall be revised to reflect both Parties' positions or removed pending resolution by the JSC at the next meeting.'

findings.clause_text: as a condition of the payment by Valeant of its share of such costs, Valeant shall have the right to review and approve (acting reasonably and in good faith) any such excess speaker programs
findings.description: Valeant's payment obligation is conditional on its approval, creating a mechanism for Valeant to avoid financial contribution by withholding approval while Dova is left to either cancel planned programs or fund them unilaterally.
findings.reasoning: The clause structures Valeant's payment as contingent on its approval of the programs. This creates timing and commitment risks: Dova must plan and possibly execute programs before knowing if Valeant will approve and pay. If Valeant withholds approval (even claiming to act reasonably), it avoids payment while Dova faces the choice of abandoning sunk costs or proceeding alone. The 'reasonable and good faith' standard is subjective and difficult to enforce, giving Valeant effective control over Dova's marketing budget for excess programs.
findings.remediation: Restructure as: (1) Valeant must approve or reject with detailed written justification within 10 business days; (2) Silence or failure to respond constitutes approval; (3) If Valeant rejects, Dova may proceed unilaterally with sole funding, or alternatively, Valeant must pay its share unless it can prove the program violates applicable law or the Agreement; (4) Remove the 'condition' language and make payment automatic upon Sub-Committee approval (unanimous) and Dova's execution, with Valeant's individual approval rights limited to specific operational parameters.

findings.clause_text: From time to time, each Party may change any of its representatives on the JSC by giving written notice to the other Party.
findings.description: Unrestricted unilateral right to change all JSC representatives simultaneously may disrupt governance continuity and institutional memory.
findings.reasoning: The provision allows either party to replace all three of its representatives at any time without restriction, transition period, or requirement to maintain continuity. This could be used tactically to reset negotiations by replacing representatives mid-process, or could result in loss of institutional knowledge about ongoing JSC decisions. While flexibility is important, complete unrestricted replacement creates governance instability.
findings.remediation: Add reasonable restrictions: (1) No more than one representative may be changed by a Party within any 30-day period without the other Party's consent; (2) Outgoing representatives must provide transition briefing to incoming representatives; (3) Changes may not be made during the pendency of a disputed matter before the JSC to prevent tactical replacement.

findings.clause_text: [NO TEXT PROVIDED - Section appears empty or undefined in source material]
findings.description: Absence of promotional materials approval process creates severe regulatory, liability, and operational exposure
findings.reasoning: In pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements, FDA regulations (21 CFR Part 202, OPDP guidelines), the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and anti-kickback statutes mandate strict control over promotional content. The complete absence of Section 4.4.1(b) content—despite the section title indicating it should govern 'Promotional Materials approval process'—creates critical gaps: (1) Valeant could disseminate non-compliant, off-label, or misleading promotional materials exposing Dova to regulatory enforcement, civil monetary penalties, exclusion from federal healthcare programs, and criminal liability; (2) Dova lacks contractual control over messaging for its own FDA-approved product, risking brand reputation damage and regulatory sanctions; (3) Unclear approval rights create operational deadlock, inter-party disputes, and delays in marketing campaigns; (4) No MLR (Medical-Legal-Regulatory) review requirements violate industry standard compliance frameworks and FDA guidance; (5) Absence of audit rights prevents Dova from monitoring Valeant's promotional activities.
findings.remediation: Negotiate immediate insertion of comprehensive approval process language: (a) Dova retains sole and absolute final approval authority over all promotional materials as the product owner and NDA holder; (b) Mandatory MLR review by both parties with strict defined timeline (e.g., 10 business days for review, deemed approved if no response by deadline); (c) Explicit criteria for rejection limited to FDA regulatory compliance, medical/scientific accuracy, consistency with approved labeling, and brand guidelines; (d) Explicit prohibition on use of any unapproved materials with immediate injunctive relief rights and indemnification for violations; (e) Escalation procedure to Joint Governance Committee for disputes with binding resolution timeline; (f) Comprehensive audit rights for Dova to review Valeant's promotional material repository, usage records, and training materials; (g) Requirement for promotional materials to be withdrawn immediately if regulatory authority questions compliance.

findings.description: Incentive compensation and detailing obligations provisions are entirely missing despite being referenced by operational clauses
findings.reasoning: Section 4.1.5 governs critical financial obligations in a co-promotion agreement where Dova (product owner) compensates Valeant (co-promoter) for detailing activities. The absence of defined terms creates unlimited exposure: (1) no caps on total incentive compensation payable; (2) undefined calculation methodology (e.g., whether based on Net Sales, prescription volume, or subjective performance); (3) no clarity on cost allocation between parties; (4) missing audit rights to verify Valeant's detailing activities claimed for compensation; (5) no termination provisions regarding accrued but unpaid incentives; (6) potential double-payment risk if obligations overlap with other sections. Without explicit language conditioning payment on actual performance of approved detailing activities, Valeant could claim entitlement to payments based on minimal or non-compliant activities.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive incentive compensation provisions including: (a) specific calculation methodology tied to measurable KPIs (e.g., Net Sales attributable to Valeant's detailing as determined by agreed allocation methodology, with explicit exclusion of samples, vouchers, and chargebacks); (b) hard annual caps on total incentive payments (e.g., not to exceed [X]% of Net Sales or $[X] annually); (c) clear allocation of costs (Dova pays incentive compensation; Valeant bears its own personnel costs unless explicitly agreed otherwise); (d) audit rights for Dova to verify detailing activities and resulting sales data; (e) termination provisions specifying that only incentives earned and verified pre-termination are payable, with post-termination wind-down limitations; (f) requirement that all detailing activities must be approved by Joint Governance Committee to qualify for compensation; (g) most favored customer clause ensuring Valeant's compensation terms are no more favorable than other co-promotion partners.

findings.clause_text: [TEXT NOT PROVIDED]
findings.description: Section 4.2.2 text is missing, preventing analysis of Additional Detailing Provisions referenced by Section 3.3.6
findings.reasoning: Section 4.2.2 is cross-referenced from Section 3.3.6, indicating it contains substantive provisions regarding detailing activities in this co-promotion agreement. Without the actual text, it is impossible to assess critical risks including: (1) allocation of detailing costs and responsibilities between Dova (product owner) and Valeant (co-promotion partner); (2) performance metrics and minimum detailing requirements that could trigger breach; (3) intellectual property ownership of detailing materials created by Valeant; (4) liability for off-label promotion or regulatory violations during detailing; (5) indemnification obligations for detailing-related claims; and (6) termination rights related to detailing performance. The absence of this text creates a critical gap in due diligence and contract risk assessment.
findings.remediation: Immediately obtain the complete executed text of Section 4.2.2 from the counterparty or contract repository before proceeding with contract execution or providing final legal clearance. Flag this as a 'showstopper' item preventing contract finalization.

findings.clause_text: As between the Parties, except as expressly set out herein, all regulatory matters regarding the Product shall be the responsibility of Dova, including responsibility for all communications with Governmental Authorities, including but not limited to FDA, related to the Product... Dova shall be responsible for any reporting of matters regarding the manufacture, sale or promotion of the Product (including Adverse Events) to or with the FDA...
findings.description: Dova bears unlimited regulatory liability without indemnification carve-out for Valeant's promotional misconduct
findings.reasoning: As the Marketing Authorization Holder, Dova appropriately holds primary regulatory responsibility. However, the clause lacks any indemnification mechanism or cost-shifting provision requiring Valeant to indemnify Dova for regulatory fines, penalties, consent decree costs, or remedial expenses arising from Valeant's promotional activities, off-label promotion, or regulatory misconduct. This exposes Dova to unlimited liability for regulatory violations caused by Valeant's detailing activities.
findings.remediation: Add indemnification provision requiring Valeant to defend and indemnify Dova against all regulatory fines, penalties, and compliance costs arising from Valeant's breach of promotional guidelines, off-label promotion, failure to follow approved labeling, or other regulatory misconduct in performing the Valeant Activities.

findings.clause_text: Valeant will not be required to engage in any Valeant Activities to the extent any finding or Government Authority has requested or suggested that Valeant may not engage in such activity.
findings.description: Valeant may unilaterally cease co-promotion based on informal regulatory suggestion
findings.reasoning: This clause allows Valeant to immediately cease all co-promotion activities (Valeant Activities) not just upon a formal regulatory order or legally binding requirement, but merely upon an informal 'request or suggestion' from a Government Authority, or even a 'finding' (which could be preliminary or informal). This creates extreme commercial uncertainty, allows Valeant to exit performance based on informal regulatory feedback, and could cripple Dova's commercialization efforts without Valeant being in breach of contract.
findings.remediation: Amend to require cessation only upon a formal written order, directive, or legally binding requirement from a Government Authority. Alternatively, require immediate consultation between parties upon any informal suggestion, with Valeant only permitted to cease specific problematic activities (not all Valeant Activities) and only after good faith discussion of remediation alternatives.

findings.clause_text: The Pharmacovigilance Agreement shall provide that: (i) Dova shall be responsible for all pharmacovigilance activities regarding the Product, including signal detection, medical surveillance, risk management, medical literature review and monitoring, Adverse Event reporting and responses to Governmental Authority requests or enquiries... and (ii) in the event Valeant receives safety information regarding the Product... Valeant shall notify Dova as soon as practicable, but, in any event, within the timelines set forth in the Pharmacovigilance Agreement.
findings.description: Dova bears all pharmacovigilance costs and liability without indemnification for Valeant's reporting failures
findings.reasoning: Dova, as MAH, appropriately holds primary PV responsibility. However, the clause lacks indemnification for regulatory fines or penalties incurred by Dova if Valeant fails to report safety information within required timelines or 'as soon as practicable.' Since Dova is responsible for all regulatory reporting to authorities, Valeant's delay could cause Dova to miss FDA deadlines (e.g., 15-day expedited reports), resulting in significant fines for which Dova has no recourse against Valeant under this clause.
findings.remediation: Add indemnification provision requiring Valeant to indemnify Dova for all regulatory fines, penalties, and costs resulting from Valeant's failure to report safety information within the timelines specified in the Pharmacovigilance Agreement or applicable law. Additionally, specify concrete maximum timeframes (e.g., 24 hours for SAEs) rather than relying solely on the separate Pharmacovigilance Agreement.

findings.clause_text: As between the Parties, Dova shall have the sole right to determine whether to implement, and to implement, a recall, field alert, withdrawal or other corrective action related to the Product. Dova shall bear the cost and expense of any such recall, field alert, withdrawal or other corrective action.
findings.description: Dova bears all recall costs without exception for Valeant-caused recalls
findings.reasoning: While Dova appropriately holds decision-making authority as MAH, the clause unconditionally requires Dova to bear all recall costs without carve-out for recalls caused by Valeant's promotional misconduct (e.g., off-label promotion leading to adverse events), regulatory violations, or negligence. This exposes Dova to significant costs for product withdrawals necessitated by Valeant's actions.
findings.remediation: Add exception to Dova's cost responsibility for recalls caused by Valeant's breach of this Agreement, promotional misconduct, off-label promotion, or regulatory violations, with Valeant required to indemnify Dova for such costs.

findings.clause_text: However, if a Party is deemed to have provided any payments or transfers of value to a Third Party on behalf of the other Party as it relates to the Product, then such Party shall provide to the other Party... the data and other information on a timely basis (i.e., in the case of manual reporting of such data and other information, within [***] following the end of each Calendar Quarter...
findings.description: Uncertain Sunshine Act liability and tight data provision timelines
findings.reasoning: The 'deemed to have provided' language creates legal uncertainty about when the obligation triggers. If Valeant is deemed to be providing payments on Dova's behalf (e.g., for speaker programs) and fails to provide the required data within the tight [***] day post-quarter timeline, Dova could face liability for incomplete or late Sunshine Act (Open Payments) reporting. The clause lacks indemnification for Valeant's failure to provide data.
findings.remediation: Clarify specific circumstances triggering the 'deemed' provision (e.g., specific types of interactions). Extend the data provision timeline or require real-time tracking. Add indemnification for failure to provide timely data resulting in reporting violations.

findings.clause_text: Dova has the right to review and comment on Valeant's draft responses to any Governmental Authorities relevant to Detail of the Product prior to Valeant's issuance of such response; and Valeant agrees to consider any comments or suggestions from Dova in good faith.
findings.description: Inadequate control over Valeant's regulatory communications
findings.reasoning: While Dova has review rights, Valeant is only required to 'consider' comments 'in good faith,' not to obtain Dova's approval or incorporate Dova's comments. This allows Valeant to proceed with regulatory communications that Dova believes are inaccurate, misleading, or harmful to the Product's regulatory status, potentially creating regulatory liability for Dova as the MAH.
findings.remediation: Change 'consider... in good faith' to 'obtain Dova's prior written approval,' which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Alternatively, require escalation to senior management if parties disagree.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall advise any customer who attempts to return any Product to Valeant (or its Affiliates) that such Product must be shipped by the customer to the facility designated by Dova... Dova shall provide to Valeant written instructions as to how Valeant should handle any Product that is actually physically returned to Valeant. Valeant shall take no other actions with respect to such return without the prior written consent of Dova.
findings.description: Product integrity and diversion risks from mishandled returns
findings.reasoning: If customers mistakenly return Product to Valeant (e.g., due to co-promotion branding confusion), and Valeant physically receives the product, there are risks of product diversion, counterfeiting, or adulteration if Valeant mishandles the product before transferring to Dova. While Valeant must follow Dova's instructions, there is no indemnification if Valeant's failure to follow instructions results in regulatory violations, patient harm, or product loss.
findings.remediation: Add specific handling requirements (e.g., immediate quarantine, secure storage, chain of custody documentation). Add indemnification for losses arising from Valeant's failure to follow Dova's instructions regarding returns.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall direct to Dova any unsolicited requests for off-label medical information... promptly following receipt by Valeant (but in no event later than [***] after receipt). Dova shall, within [***] following receipt of any such request from Valeant, address any such requests directly.
findings.description: Compressed timelines for off-label medical information responses create compliance risk
findings.reasoning: Dova is contractually bound to respond to off-label medical information requests within [***] days of receipt from Valeant. If Valeant delays forwarding the request (using the maximum [***] days allowed), Dova has severely limited time to prepare a medically accurate, compliant response. Failure to respond appropriately to off-label requests can result in FDA enforcement action for misbranding or off-label promotion.
findings.remediation: Require Valeant to forward requests within 24 hours. Extend Dova's response time to [***] days from Valeant's receipt, not Dova's receipt. Alternatively, specify that Dova's obligation is to use commercially reasonable efforts to respond within the timeframe, not an absolute obligation.

findings.clause_text: Other than as set forth in this Agreement, Dova shall be responsible for all marketing of the Product in the Territory, provided that Dova shall continue to invest in marketing that is targeted towards the Specialty.
findings.description: Vague ongoing marketing investment obligation
findings.reasoning: The clause requires Dova to 'continue to invest in marketing' targeted towards the Specialty without defining minimum spend, specific metrics, or duration. This creates an ambiguous contractual obligation that could be interpreted as a material covenant, potentially giving Valeant grounds to claim breach if Dova reduces marketing spend in the Specialty based on commercial judgment, even if the co-promotion agreement otherwise allows for such adjustments.
findings.remediation: Clarify that marketing investments are subject to Dova's commercially reasonable discretion and overall business strategy, or specify minimum marketing spend amounts or metrics (e.g., 'consistent with the marketing plan attached as Exhibit X').

findings.clause_text: If Valeant receives an order for the Product, it shall promptly transmit such order to Dova (or its designee) for acceptance or rejection.
findings.description: Lack of specific order transmission SLA
findings.reasoning: While Valeant must 'promptly transmit' orders to Dova, the lack of a specific service level agreement (e.g., within 24 hours) creates operational risk. Delays in order transmission could result in lost sales, customer dissatisfaction, or supply chain disruptions for which Dova bears the commercial consequences (as Dova records the revenue and manages inventory).
findings.remediation: Specify a strict timeline for order transmission (e.g., 'within 24 hours of receipt' or 'same business day').

findings.clause_text: [Section content not provided - referenced in Sections 5.7 and 5.9 regarding indemnification provisions]
findings.description: Missing critical indemnification provisions create unquantified regulatory liability exposure
findings.reasoning: Section 12.6 is cross-referenced from Sections 5.7 and 5.9 as containing indemnification provisions critical to assessing regulatory liability gaps. In a pharmaceutical co-promotion agreement, indemnification provisions allocate responsibility for FDA enforcement actions, off-label promotion claims, adverse event reporting failures, and product liability. Without visibility into these provisions, Dova cannot assess whether it is required to indemnify Valeant for regulatory violations arising from Valeant's promotional activities, whether liability caps exist, or whether Dova has reciprocal indemnification rights. This creates unquantified financial and regulatory exposure.
findings.remediation: Immediately request full text of Section 12.6. Negotiate for: (1) Mutual indemnification with carve-outs for each party's negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of regulatory requirements; (2) Specific indemnification by Valeant for regulatory violations, FDA enforcement actions, and off-label promotion claims arising from Valeant's promotional activities; (3) Liability caps on aggregate indemnification obligations (e.g., capped at fees paid or a fixed amount); (4) Exclusion of indemnification for claims arising from the indemnified party's breach of the agreement or applicable law; (5) Right to control defense of regulatory actions affecting product approval.

findings.clause_text: [Not provided - described as containing provisions 'critical to assessing whether regulatory liability gaps are covered']
findings.description: Uncertainty regarding specific regulatory liability gaps and safety reporting indemnification
findings.reasoning: The meta-description of Section 12.6 explicitly references 'regulatory liability gaps,' indicating the drafters identified specific uncovered risks. In pharmaceutical co-promotion, critical gaps typically include: (a) FDA enforcement actions (Warning Letters, consent decrees, debarment); (b) off-label promotion liability under False Claims Act; (c) adverse event reporting and pharmacovigilance failures; (d) pricing/reimbursement fraud; (e) clinical trial misconduct; and (f) product liability for safety issues. Without the specific allocation of these risks in Section 12.6, Dova cannot determine its exposure for Valeant's promotional conduct or safety reporting obligations.
findings.remediation: Ensure Section 12.6 explicitly addresses: (1) Allocation of costs and penalties for FDA enforcement actions, including consent decrees and debarment; (2) Clear responsibility for adverse event reporting and pharmacovigilance (typically retained by product owner Dova, but Valeant must report to Dova); (3) Indemnification by Valeant for off-label promotion claims tied specifically to Valeant's sales representatives' activities; (4) Exclusion of consequential damages for regulatory delays or market withdrawals; (5) Right to control defense of regulatory actions affecting product approval (should remain with Dova as product owner); (6) Specific carve-out for liability arising from Valeant's failure to follow Dova's approved promotional materials or regulatory guidance.

findings.clause_text: Section 12.6 (referenced in Sections 5.7 and 5.9) - Likely contains indemnification provisions critical to assessing whether regulatory liability gaps are covered
findings.description: Circular cross-referencing between regulatory obligations and indemnification creates interpretive ambiguity
findings.reasoning: The provided cross-reference map indicates circular dependencies: Section 12.6 is referenced in Sections 5.7 and 5.9, while 12.6 apparently references back to 5.7 and 5.9. This circularity creates ambiguity regarding which provisions control the scope of indemnification. If Sections 5.7 and 5.9 define substantive regulatory compliance obligations (e.g., safety reporting, promotional material approval) while Section 12.6 defines indemnification for breaches thereof, circular referencing could lead to: (a) conflicting interpretations of which party bears liability for regulatory failures; (b) gaps where neither party accepts indemnification responsibility; or (c) overlapping obligations creating duplicate liability exposure.
findings.remediation: Clarify the hierarchy and eliminate circularity: (1) Amend Sections 5.7 and 5.9 to state that indemnification for regulatory breaches is governed exclusively by Section 12.6; (2) Amend Section 12.6 to confirm it controls over conflicting provisions in Sections 5.7 and 5.9 regarding liability allocation; (3) Remove reciprocal references between 12.6 and 5.7/5.9, making the relationship unidirectional (substantive obligations in 5.7/5.9, indemnification in 12.6); (4) Add explicit language that in case of conflict between indemnification provisions, Section 12.6 prevails.

findings.description: Missing definition text for critical regulatory terms ('Adverse Events', 'Product') prevents assessment of safety reporting obligations and liability scope.
findings.reasoning: Section 1.2 defines 'Adverse Events' and 'Product' which are referenced in Section 5.4 (Regulatory/Safety). Without the actual definition text, it is impossible to verify whether the definitions are overly broad (e.g., including product quality complaints, overdose, or off-label use as 'Adverse Events'), which would impose excessive reporting burdens and liability on Dova. In co-promotion agreements, the scope of 'Adverse Events' directly impacts pharmacovigilance obligations and indemnification exposure.
findings.remediation: Request the complete text of Section 1.2. Ensure 'Adverse Events' is narrowly defined per ICH E2A guidelines (unfavorable medical occurrence in a patient administered a pharmaceutical product, not necessarily causally related). Explicitly exclude: (a) product quality complaints not involving safety, (b) overdose without clinical consequence, (c) off-label use unless resulting in harm. Ensure 'Product' is limited to specific NDCs, formulations, and approved indications covered by the agreement.

findings.description: The definition of 'Valeant Activities' is entirely missing from the agreement text, creating critical ambiguity regarding the scope of Valeant's obligations and cessation rights under Section 5.3.
findings.reasoning: In a co-promotion agreement, the definition of the co-promotion partner's activities is fundamental to determining commercial obligations, performance metrics, and conditions for cessation. Without this definition, Dova Pharmaceuticals cannot enforce Valeant's obligations, measure performance against KPIs, or determine when unilateral cessation is permitted. The cross-reference pattern (5.4 -> 1.2 as_defined_in) suggests the definition should reside in Section 1.2, but its absence creates unilateral exposure where Valeant could interpret 'activities' narrowly to minimize obligations or broadly to justify early cessation.
findings.remediation: Insert a comprehensive definition of 'Valeant Activities' in Section 1.2 that specifically enumerates: (1) detailed promotional, marketing, detailing, and sales activities Valeant must perform; (2) specific territories, channels, and customer segments covered; (3) quantifiable performance metrics, call frequencies, and KPIs; (4) required compliance standards and regulatory obligations; (5) minimum resource commitments (FTEs, budget); and (6) excluded activities. Ensure Section 5.3 cross-references this definition for cessation triggers.

findings.description: The provided contract text includes the Table of Contents referencing 'ARTICLE 1 DEFINITIONS' at page 1, but the actual definitional content of Article 1 is not included in the provided text. Without the specific defined terms (e.g., 'Product,' 'Territory,' 'Field Force,' 'Detailing,' 'Promotion Fee,' 'JSC'), it is impossible to analyze how these terms modify contractual obligations, limit or expand scope, or allocate risk between Dova and Valeant.

findings.clause_text: Any obligation of Valeant under or pursuant to this Agreement may be satisfied, met or fulfilled, in whole or in part, at Valeant's sole and exclusive option, either by Valeant or its Affiliates.
findings.description: Valeant may utilize any Affiliate to perform co-promotion obligations without Dova's prior approval, creating change-of-control and performance risks.
findings.reasoning: The combination of 'sole and exclusive option' language with the absence of prior approval rights for Dova means Valeant could engage Affiliates that are competitors of Dova, have poor regulatory compliance histories, or are located outside the Territory without Dova's consent. If Valeant is acquired, the new controlling entity's subsidiaries automatically become permissible Affiliates, potentially transferring co-promotion rights to a competitor or undesirable party without Dova's consent, despite the non-assignment language.
findings.remediation: Amend to require Dova's prior written approval for each Affiliate performing obligations, with approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned on the Affiliate meeting Dova's compliance and qualification standards. Alternatively, add a change-of-control provision requiring Dova's consent to continue the Agreement if Valeant is acquired by a competitor or entity with poor regulatory standing.

findings.clause_text: Valeant guarantees the performance of all actions, agreements and obligations to be performed by its Affiliates under the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
findings.description: While Valeant guarantees Affiliate performance, Dova lacks explicit audit rights to verify Affiliate compliance directly.
findings.reasoning: The guarantee of performance is enforceable only to the extent Dova can detect non-performance. Without explicit rights to audit Affiliates (not just Valeant), Dova may be unable to discover breaches by Affiliates—such as off-label promotion, improper safety reporting, or unauthorized use of trademarks—until they result in regulatory enforcement or significant brand damage. This undermines the effectiveness of the performance guarantee.
findings.remediation: Add explicit audit rights permitting Dova to inspect Affiliate records and activities related to the Agreement, with reasonable advance notice and at Dova's cost (or at Valeant's cost if material breaches are discovered).

findings.clause_text: responsibility for all decisions regarding regulatory submissions and, except as expressly set forth herein, for interactions with any Governmental Authority, including but not limited to FDA, with respect to the Product;
findings.description: Ambiguous exception to Dova's exclusive regulatory authority creates uncertainty regarding Valeant's permitted interactions with Governmental Authorities.
findings.reasoning: The phrase 'except as expressly set forth herein' suggests that Valeant may have specific rights to interact with FDA or other authorities in certain contexts (possibly related to the institutional account management team referenced in Sections 2.1 and 2.2.6). Unclear allocation of regulatory communication rights creates risk of conflicting submissions, unauthorized representations to FDA, or regulatory enforcement action if Valeant oversteps its authority. This is particularly critical in pharmaceutical co-promotions where off-label promotion or inconsistent safety messaging can trigger FDA enforcement.
findings.remediation: Specify the exact circumstances (e.g., specific types of inquiries, specific agencies, or specific sections like 4.1.5) where Valeant may interact with Governmental Authorities, or require Dova's prior approval for any such interactions.

findings.clause_text: responsibility for final approval of all Product Materials content (including submission of Promotional Materials to FDA's Office of Prescription Drug Promotion) with respect to the conduct of the Valeant Activities for Product, except as expressly set forth herein;
findings.description: Unspecified exceptions to Dova's final approval authority over promotional materials create risk of unauthorized marketing content.
findings.reasoning: While Dova retains final approval rights over Product Materials, the 'except as expressly set forth herein' qualifier indicates that certain materials or circumstances may be exempt from this approval requirement. Without knowing the scope of these exceptions (which may be in Section 4.1.5 regarding institutional accounts or elsewhere), Dova faces uncertainty regarding what materials Valeant may use without approval. This creates regulatory risk if Valeant uses unapproved materials that contain off-label claims, misleading information, or non-compliant messaging.
findings.remediation: Clarify the scope of exceptions by referencing specific section numbers or limiting exceptions to specific pre-approved categories (e.g., Valeant's corporate materials that do not mention the Product or specific pre-approved templates).

findings.clause_text: responsibility for handling all safety related activities related to Product as set forth in ARTICLE 5 (including submitting all safety reports and interacting with Governmental Authorities with respect thereto) and initiating and managing any Product recalls.
findings.description: Dova bears sole responsibility for pharmacovigilance and recalls arising from promotional activities conducted by Valeant, without explicit indemnification or cost-sharing for Valeant-caused safety issues.
findings.reasoning: As the MA holder, Dova appropriately retains safety responsibility. However, if safety issues, adverse events, or recalls arise from Valeant's promotional activities (e.g., off-label promotion leading to adverse events, improper dosing recommendations by Valeant representatives), Dova bears the regulatory burden and costs of managing the recall and safety reporting without explicit contractual indemnification or cost-sharing from Valeant. This creates significant financial and regulatory exposure for Dova for Valeant's misconduct.
findings.remediation: Add provision requiring Valeant to indemnify Dova for all costs, expenses, and liabilities associated with recalls, safety reporting, or regulatory enforcement actions arising from Valeant's negligence, misconduct, or breach of the Agreement, including off-label promotion or failure to follow approved materials.

findings.clause_text: [Section 2.4 generally - absence of indemnification for third-party IP claims]
findings.description: Article 2.4 extensively regulates trademark use but omits indemnification for third-party claims arising from Valeant's promotional activities.
findings.reasoning: While Section 2.4 imposes numerous obligations on Valeant regarding use of Dova's trademarks, it fails to require Valeant to indemnify Dova against third-party claims (e.g., trademark infringement by third parties claiming Valeant's promotional materials infringe their marks, copyright infringement in materials created by Valeant, false advertising claims arising from Valeant's promotional content). This leaves Dova exposed to liability for Valeant's creative and promotional decisions without contractual recourse for indemnification, forcing Dova to bear legal defense costs and damages even when Valeant created the offending materials.
findings.remediation: Add indemnification clause requiring Valeant to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Dova from any third-party claims arising from Valeant's use of trademarks, creation of Product Materials, or promotional activities under the Agreement, except for claims arising from Dova's final approved content.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall promptly notify Dova upon becoming aware of any violation of this Section 2.4.1.
findings.description: Notification obligation is artificially limited to violations of Section 2.4.1 only, excluding violations of Section 2.4.2 and broader trademark obligations.
findings.reasoning: Valeant is contractually obligated to notify Dova only of violations of the specific usage grant in Section 2.4.1, but not of violations of the quality control, non-contest, non-impairment, or other protective obligations in Section 2.4.2. This creates a monitoring gap where Dova may not learn of material breaches—such as Valeant contesting Dova's trademark ownership, using confusingly similar marks, or negligently impairing Dova's rights—until significant damage has occurred, potentially prejudicing Dova's legal position or causing irreparable harm to the brand.
findings.remediation: Expand the notification obligation to cover any violation of Article 2.4 (Trademarks and Copyrights) or the Agreement generally, or specifically list Sections 2.4.1 and 2.4.2 in the notification obligation.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall not at any time during the Term knowingly do or allow to be done any act or thing which will in any way impair or diminish the rights of Dova in or to the Dova Trademarks and Copyrights.
findings.description: The 'knowingly' mens rea requirement limits Valeant's liability for impairment of Dova's intellectual property rights to intentional acts only, excluding negligence.
findings.reasoning: By restricting the prohibition to 'knowingly' impairing rights, the clause effectively permits Valeant to negligently or recklessly damage Dova's trademark rights without contractual breach. In pharmaceutical co-promotions, this creates significant exposure: Valeant could negligently use the marks in a manner that causes genericide (loss of trademark distinctiveness), make unauthorized modifications to logos that dilute the mark, or fail to supervise representatives leading to misuse, all without breaching this clause unless Dova can prove intent. Proving intentional impairment is significantly more difficult than proving negligence, creating enforcement gaps.
findings.remediation: Remove 'knowingly' to impose strict liability for any act that impairs Dova's rights, or replace with 'knowingly or negligently' to cover both intentional and careless acts.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall also adhere to at least the same quality control provisions as companies in the pharmaceutical industry adhere to for their own trademarks and copyrights.
findings.description: Quality control standard references an undefined, floating 'pharmaceutical industry' standard rather than Dova's specific, binding trademark guidelines.
findings.reasoning: The phrase 'companies in the pharmaceutical industry' creates an ambiguous, subjective standard that varies widely between companies. Without specific reference to Dova's trademark usage guidelines (which are mentioned earlier in 2.4.2 but not incorporated as the binding standard), Dova faces difficulty enforcing specific quality requirements. Valeant could argue its practices meet the standard of some pharmaceutical companies even if they fall below Dova's specific requirements or FDA promotional guidelines, potentially leading to trademark dilution, regulatory enforcement, or loss of trademark rights due to inadequate quality control (which is required to maintain trademark validity).
findings.remediation: Replace the floating standard with specific reference to 'Dova's then-current trademark and copyright usage guidelines, as provided to Valeant in writing and updated periodically, which shall meet or exceed industry standards' and require written acknowledgment of updates.

findings.clause_text: institutional account management team activities and any Governmental Authority interaction rights
findings.description: Unilateral rights to interact with Governmental Authorities without joint control or prior approval from Product Owner
findings.reasoning: In a co-promotion agreement, allowing the co-promotion partner (Valeant) unilateral rights to interact with FDA and other regulatory authorities creates significant compliance and liability risks for Dova as the NDA holder. The partner could make representations, commitments, or disclosures that bind Dova, trigger reporting obligations, or create adverse regulatory precedents without Dova's knowledge or consent.
findings.remediation: Amend to require joint decision-making for all Governmental Authority interactions, with Dova having final approval rights as the product owner/NDA holder. Require prior written consent for any regulatory communications and mandatory presence of Dova representatives in any meetings with authorities.

findings.clause_text: institutional account management team activities
findings.description: Unclear scope and control of institutional account management activities creating operational and compliance conflicts
findings.reasoning: Without clear definition of 'institutional account management team activities,' Valeant could interpret this broadly to include activities that conflict with Dova's overall commercial strategy or compliance protocols. This could lead to inconsistent messaging to institutional customers (hospitals, GPOs, etc.), potential anti-kickback statute violations if activities are not coordinated, and confusion regarding which party bears responsibility for specific account management functions.
findings.remediation: Define specific scope of institutional account management activities with clear boundaries, require adherence to Dova's compliance policies and procedures, mandate coordination of messaging and strategy, and specify that Dova retains oversight and approval rights over account plans for major institutional customers.

findings.clause_text: any Governmental Authority interaction rights
findings.description: Absence of notification and information sharing requirements regarding regulatory interactions
findings.reasoning: Even if joint control is established, the lack of explicit notification requirements means Valeant could engage with authorities without promptly informing Dova, preventing Dova from taking necessary compliance actions or preparing appropriate responses. This creates gaps in pharmacovigilance, adverse event reporting, and regulatory intelligence sharing that are critical for pharmaceutical co-promotion arrangements.
findings.remediation: Add explicit language requiring immediate (within 24 hours) notification of any Governmental Authority contact, inquiry, or inspection, along with full disclosure of all communications and documents exchanged. Require periodic reporting of all regulatory interactions and establish a joint regulatory affairs committee to coordinate strategy.

findings.description: Section referenced in cross-references but lacks defined substantive provisions
findings.reasoning: Section 4.1.5 is referenced by multiple other sections (2.1, 2.2) suggesting it contains material rights or obligations, yet the text is undefined or missing. This creates uncertainty regarding the scope of rights granted regarding institutional account management and governmental authority interactions, potentially leading to disputes over interpretation or unintended broad grants of authority to Valeant.
findings.remediation: Ensure comprehensive drafting of Section 4.1.5 with specific limitations on governmental authority interactions, clear definitions of institutional account management scope, and explicit approval rights for Dova. Do not execute agreement with this section undefined.

findings.clause_text: [EMPTY - Section 4.4 text not provided or blank]
findings.description: Missing trademark ownership and maintenance provisions
findings.reasoning: Section 4.4 is referenced in Section 2.4.1 regarding trademark updates or ownership, but the section text is empty. In a co-promotion agreement where Dova is the product owner and Valeant the co-promotion partner, clear ownership of product trademarks is essential to protect Dova's core IP assets. Without defined provisions, Dova's ownership rights may be challenged, and obligations for trademark prosecution, maintenance, defense, and associated costs remain unallocated. This creates significant exposure regarding intellectual property rights that are central to the co-promotion arrangement and could result in loss of trademark protection or unbudgeted prosecution costs.
findings.remediation: Negotiate to include comprehensive trademark provisions: (1) Explicit confirmation that Dova retains sole and exclusive ownership of all product trademarks and associated goodwill; (2) Grant to Valeant of a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use trademarks solely for co-promotion activities during the term, subject to Dova's quality control guidelines; (3) Clear allocation of responsibility and costs for trademark prosecution, maintenance, renewals, and defense of infringement claims (typically borne by owner Dova, but costs of defense for claims arising from Valeant's activities should be borne by Valeant); (4) Requirement for Valeant to notify Dova immediately of any suspected infringement or challenge to trademark validity; (5) Post-termination obligations requiring immediate cessation of use and destruction of materials bearing marks.

findings.clause_text: [EMPTY - Section 4.4 text not provided or blank]
findings.description: Ambiguity in trademark use rights and quality control for co-promotion partner
findings.reasoning: Without explicit language governing Valeant's use of Dova's trademarks in co-promotion activities, there is no contractual restriction on the scope, manner, territory, or quality control of such use. Under trademark law, uncontrolled licensing (naked licensing) can result in loss of trademark rights due to abandonment. Additionally, without quality control provisions, Valeant's use of the marks in a manner that diminishes quality could damage Dova's brand reputation. There is also no restriction preventing Valeant from using the marks for products outside the scope of the co-promotion or continuing use after termination, which could create confusion as to the source of goods and dilute Dova's trademark rights.
findings.remediation: Insert specific trademark license grant and quality control provisions: 'Subject to the terms hereof, Dova grants Valeant a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license during the Term to use the Product Trademarks solely in connection with the Co-Promotion Activities in the Territory and only in accordance with Dova's trademark usage guidelines provided herein or as otherwise approved in writing by Dova. Valeant shall maintain the quality of goods and services offered under the Product Trademarks in accordance with Dova's quality standards. Dova shall have the right to inspect and approve any materials bearing the Product Trademarks prior to use. All goodwill generated by Valeant's use of the Product Trademarks shall inure solely to Dova's benefit. Valeant shall not register or attempt to register any trademark, service mark, or domain name confusingly similar to the Product Trademarks.'

findings.clause_text: [EMPTY - Section 4.4 text not provided or blank]
findings.description: Missing trademark indemnification and infringement defense obligations
findings.reasoning: The absence of trademark-specific indemnification provisions leaves Dova exposed to significant liability for third-party infringement claims arising from Valeant's co-promotion activities without contractual recourse against Valeant. In pharmaceutical co-promotion, trademark disputes can be extremely costly and damaging to brand reputation. Without indemnification, Dova could bear the full cost of defending claims that Valeant's marketing materials or activities infringed third-party trademarks, or that Valeant's use of Dova's marks caused confusion. Conversely, there is no protection for Valeant for claims arising from Dova's pre-existing trademark rights, though this is less critical for Dova's risk profile. There is also no allocation of control of defense strategy for infringement litigation, which is critical for Dova to protect its brand integrity.
findings.remediation: Add mutual indemnification specific to IP: 'Each party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to any third-party claim alleging infringement of trademark, trade name, or service mark rights arising from the indemnifying party's activities, marketing materials, or use of marks under this Agreement. Dova shall have sole control of the defense of any claim challenging the validity or ownership of the Product Trademarks or alleging that the Product Trademarks infringe third-party rights, provided that Valeant shall cooperate in such defense at Dova's request. Valeant shall promptly notify Dova in writing of any suspected infringement of the Product Trademarks by third parties or any challenge to the validity of such marks.'

findings.clause_text: [EMPTY - Section 4.4 text not provided or blank]
findings.description: Missing post-termination trademark use restrictions and transition obligations
findings.reasoning: Without explicit post-termination obligations regarding trademark use, Valeant may theoretically continue to use Dova's trademarks after the co-promotion relationship ends, creating confusion in the marketplace, diluting Dova's brand, and potentially causing patients or healthcare providers to believe Valeant remains affiliated with the product. There are no provisions requiring destruction of materials bearing the trademarks, return of confidential trademark guidelines, or transition periods for phase-out of use. This could result in unauthorized use that Dova must address through costly cease-and-desist efforts or litigation after termination.
findings.remediation: Include survival and transition provisions: 'Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Valeant shall immediately cease all use of the Product Trademarks and shall not thereafter use, register, or attempt to register any mark confusingly similar thereto. Valeant shall return or destroy all materials bearing the Product Trademarks and confirm such destruction in writing within thirty (30) days of termination. Valeant shall not claim any rights in or to the Product Trademarks by virtue of its use hereunder, and all goodwill associated with Valeant's use shall remain with Dova. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Valeant may continue to sell existing inventory bearing the Product Trademarks for a period not exceeding ninety (90) days post-termination, provided such sales do not create confusion as to the parties' current relationship and Valeant provides appropriate notice to customers regarding the terminated relationship.'

findings.clause_ref: Article 5 (safety reporting and pharmacovigilance obligations referenced in Section 2.2.6)
findings.description: Missing pharmacovigilance clause text creates severe regulatory compliance and patient safety liability exposure
findings.reasoning: Article 5 governs safety reporting and pharmacovigilance (PV) obligations, which are mission-critical in pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements. As the Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH), Dova retains primary legal responsibility to FDA/EMA for adverse event (AE) reporting, signal detection, and risk management. The absence of this text prevents assessment of whether: (1) Valeant is obligated to report AEs to Dova within regulatory timelines (24-hour/15-day windows); (2) Dova retains exclusive authority to submit reports to regulators; (3) Valeant's independent promotional activities create PV gaps; or (4) Dova has audit rights over Valeant's AE collection. Missing or inadequate PV obligations expose Dova to regulatory enforcement, consent decrees, criminal liability, and patient safety litigation.
findings.remediation: Immediately obtain and negotiate full text of Article 5. Ensure provisions: (a) Designate Dova as sole PV responsible party to regulators; (b) Require Valeant to forward all AEs to Dova within 24 hours of receipt; (c) Prohibit Valeant from independent regulatory reporting; (d) Grant Dova audit rights over Valeant's AE databases and promotional materials; (e) Include indemnification for PV failures caused by Valeant; (f) Specify signal detection and risk management authority resides solely with Dova; (g) Address social media and digital promotion AE monitoring obligations.

findings.clause_text: Other than as expressly stated herein, Valeant shall not be required to modify its compliance policies or practices in connection with the compliance-related provisions herein.
findings.description: Valeant is contractually excused from modifying its compliance policies to meet Product-specific requirements or Dova's reasonable requests.
findings.reasoning: This creates significant regulatory exposure for Dova as the product owner. If Valeant's existing compliance policies are inadequate for the specific Product (e.g., REMS requirements, specialized anti-kickback protocols), Dova cannot contractually compel updates, yet Dova will bear primary regulatory liability for any resulting violations.
findings.remediation: Delete this carve-out. Require Valeant to maintain compliance policies that are appropriate for the Product and comply with all Applicable Laws, and to modify them as necessary to address Product-specific requirements or Dova's reasonable requests based on regulatory guidance.

findings.clause_text: If the Compliance Managers do not reach consensus on an issue promptly, then such issue shall be submitted to dispute resolution process described in Section 13.6.
findings.description: The term 'promptly' is undefined, creating uncertainty regarding when compliance disputes escalate to formal resolution.
findings.reasoning: Without a defined timeframe (e.g., 5 business days), Valeant could delay consensus indefinitely while claiming good faith negotiations, preventing Dova from accessing formal dispute resolution and potentially allowing ongoing compliance violations to persist unremedied.
findings.remediation: Define 'promptly' as a specific number of business days (e.g., 'within five (5) Business Days').

findings.clause_text: If, during the Term, Valeant becomes aware of a material violation or failure to comply with Applicable Law or the terms of this Agreement by a member of the Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing...
findings.description: Notification obligation is limited to Field Force Personnel engaged in 'Detailing,' excluding other personnel performing Valeant Activities.
findings.reasoning: Field Force Personnel may engage in activities beyond Detailing (e.g., market access, reimbursement support, non-personal promotion). Violations by these personnel (e.g., improper HUB interactions, off-label digital marketing) would not trigger Valeant's notification obligation, creating significant compliance blind spots for Dova.
findings.remediation: Expand the obligation to cover all 'Field Force Personnel' performing any Valeant Activities, not just those engaged in Detailing.

findings.clause_text: becomes aware of a material violation or failure to comply with Applicable Law...
findings.description: The term 'material' is subjective and undefined, allowing Valeant to determine what constitutes a reportable violation.
findings.reasoning: Valeant could interpret 'material' narrowly to exclude significant compliance deviations (e.g., isolated off-label promotion, minor kickback violations), delaying or preventing Dova's awareness of issues that could expose Dova to regulatory liability as the product owner.
findings.remediation: Remove 'material' or define it to include any violation of healthcare laws, off-label promotion, or kickback violations, regardless of scale.

findings.clause_text: The entire clause imposes notification obligations solely on Valeant.
findings.description: The notification obligation is one-sided, with no reciprocal obligation for Dova to notify Valeant of violations by Dova's sales representatives.
findings.reasoning: While Dova bears primary regulatory responsibility, Valeant's Field Force interacts with Dova's representatives. If Dova's representatives violate laws (e.g., providing off-label information to Valeant's force), Valeant should be notified to protect itself and ensure coordinated compliance. The asymmetry creates an information imbalance.
findings.remediation: Add reciprocal language requiring Dova to notify Valeant of material violations by Dova's sales representatives in connection with Product promotion.

findings.clause_text: Valeant's or Dova's material failure to abide by the provisions of this Section 4.3 shall be deemed a material breach of this Agreement by Valeant or Dova (as the case may be) and subject to the terms of Section 12.2 hereof.
findings.description: Any material failure under Section 4.3 is immediately deemed a material breach without opportunity for cure, subjecting Dova to immediate termination under Section 12.2.
findings.reasoning: Section 4.3 contains numerous detailed compliance obligations. A 'material failure' could include a single instance of non-compliance or a delayed notification under 4.3.10. Without a cure period (unless Section 12.2 provides one, which is not visible here), Dova could face immediate termination of the co-promotion agreement for a remediable compliance issue, disrupting commercialization.
findings.remediation: Add a cure period (e.g., 30 days) for material failures to abide by Section 4.3, provided the failure is curable. Specify that only uncured failures constitute material breaches.

findings.clause_text: material failure to abide by the provisions of this Section 4.3
findings.description: The term 'material failure' is undefined, leaving discretion to determine what constitutes a breach triggering termination rights.
findings.reasoning: This subjectivity allows either party to characterize minor compliance deviations as 'material' to justify termination or leverage renegotiation, creating uncertainty and potential for dispute.
findings.remediation: Define 'material failure' as a failure that results in or is likely to result in regulatory enforcement action, significant financial penalty, or reputational harm.

findings.clause_text: Notwithstanding the immediately preceding sentence, Dova shall have no liability wit.. not be responsible to Valeant, or to the Field Force Personnel, for any compensation, expense reimbursements or benefits (including vacation and holiday remuneration, healthcare coverage or insurance, life insurance, severance or termination of employment benefits, pension or profit-sharing benefits and disability benefits), payroll-related taxes or withholdings, or any governmental charges or benefits (including unemployment and disability insurance contributions or benefits and workmen's compensation contributions or benefits) that may be imposed upon or be related to the performance by Valeant or such individuals of this Agreement, all of which shall be the sole responsibility of Valeant, even if it is subsequently determined by any Governmental Authority that any such individual may be an employee or a common law employee of Dova or any of its Affiliates or is otherwise entitled to such payments and benefits.
findings.description: Dova attempts to contractually disclaim all employment-related liability for Field Force Personnel even if a governmental authority determines they are Dova's common law employees.
findings.reasoning: This is an extremely broad liability shift. While Valeant is the formal employer, co-promotion arrangements create joint employment risks. If a court or agency finds joint employment (common in pharmaceutical co-promotion), this clause attempts to make Valeant solely responsible for all back taxes, benefits, penalties, etc. However, Dova might still face regulatory liability for the acts of these employees regardless of contractual allocation. The clause may be unenforceable in some jurisdictions (e.g., California, Massachusetts) where joint employment findings cannot be contractually disclaimed, potentially rendering the entire provision void or creating uncertainty.
findings.remediation: Narrow the disclaimer to apply only to the extent Valeant is determined to be the sole employer, or limit it to payroll taxes/benefits costs specifically. Add language that Dova will reimburse Valeant for any such costs attributable to Dova's specific direction/control over the personnel (if applicable). Alternatively, cap Dova's liability at a specific amount or require Valeant to maintain employment practices liability insurance. Most importantly, add a clause stating that the allocation does not affect Dova's regulatory obligations or rights to terminate for compliance violations.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall have no liability wit.. not be responsible
findings.description: The clause text appears corrupted or incomplete ('wit..'), creating ambiguity about the scope of the liability disclaimer.
findings.reasoning: The ellipsis suggests missing text that might qualify the disclaimer. Without the full text, Dova cannot assess the full scope of the liability being disclaimed or whether there are exceptions.
findings.remediation: Obtain the complete, uncorrupted text of Section 4.3.7 to verify the exact scope of the liability disclaimer.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall ensure that any patient assistance program used in connection with the Product (and the services performed thereby in connection with the Product) shall be operated in accordance with Applicable Law.
findings.description: Dova bears sole responsibility for patient assistance program compliance without apparent Valeant accountability for Field Force interactions with such programs.
findings.reasoning: Valeant's Field Force Personnel may interact with patient assistance programs (e.g., referring patients, providing information). While Dova operates the program, Valeant's personnel could create liability through improper referrals or inducements. The clause imposes absolute compliance obligation on Dova without requiring Valeant to ensure its personnel comply with program rules or limiting Dova's liability for Valeant's actions in this context.
findings.remediation: Add language requiring Valeant to ensure its Field Force Personnel comply with all patient assistance program policies and procedures established by Dova, and require Valeant to indemnify Dova for violations caused by Valeant's personnel.

findings.clause_text: (f) Valeant shall be solely responsible for the acts or omissions of the Field Force Personnel that are not in compliance with Applicable Law and the terms of this Agreement while performing any of the activities under this Agreement.
findings.description: Reinforces absolute liability on Valeant for Field Force Personnel acts without preserving Dova's regulatory rights or immediate intervention authority.
findings.reasoning: While allocating liability to the employer is standard, this clause combined with 4.5.3 (Valeant sole discretion on discipline) could prevent Dova from taking immediate action to stop violations (e.g., removing personnel from Product promotion) while waiting for Valeant to act. Dova retains regulatory liability as product owner and needs the right to immediately exclude non-compliant personnel regardless of Valeant's disciplinary process.
findings.remediation: Add language preserving Dova's right to immediately require removal of any Field Force Personnel from Product-related activities upon Dova's reasonable belief of violation, pending Valeant's investigation, without limiting Dova's right to terminate the Agreement for such violations.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall, to the extent consistent with, and in a manner similar to, its practices with respect to departures of the sales representatives or other field force personnel, as applicable, promoting, marketing or detailing other products for Valeant, account for, and shall cause such departing Field Force Personnel to return to Valeant and delete from his/her computer files...
findings.description: Return of confidential materials is governed by Valeant's internal practices, which may be inadequate, with no Dova audit rights.
findings.reasoning: Valeant's standard practices may not meet Dova's data security requirements or regulatory standards for this specific Product. The phrase 'to the extent consistent with' suggests Valeant may not fully comply if its practices are lax. Without audit rights, Dova cannot verify that proprietary account-level information and Product Materials have been properly returned or destroyed, creating ongoing confidentiality and data security risks.
findings.remediation: Replace with specific, objective requirements: (i) return all physical materials within 24 hours of termination, (ii) delete electronic files and provide written certification of deletion within 24 hours, (iii) specify exact categories of materials. Add Dova audit rights to verify compliance.

findings.clause_text: If Dova has a reasonable basis for believing any member of the Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing has violated any Applicable Laws...
findings.description: Dova's right to trigger investigation is limited to 'reasonable basis,' a subjective standard, and limited to personnel engaged in 'Detailing.'
findings.reasoning: The limitation to 'Detailing' personnel (as opposed to all Field Force Personnel) creates a gap where Dova cannot trigger investigation for violations by personnel engaged in other Valeant Activities (e.g., market access). The 'reasonable basis' standard, while subjective, is less concerning than the scope limitation.
findings.remediation: Expand the scope to all Field Force Personnel performing Valeant Activities, not just those engaged in Detailing. Define 'reasonable basis' as 'credible evidence or good faith belief based on specific facts.'

findings.clause_text: Subject to the foregoing, Valeant shall be solely responsible for taking any disciplinary actions in connection with its Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing.
findings.description: Valeant has sole discretion over disciplinary actions, with no requirement to consult Dova or follow Dova's recommendations on remedial measures.
findings.reasoning: While Valeant is the employer, Dova bears regulatory risk as the product owner. If Valeant's 'appropriate remedial action' is insufficient (e.g., verbal warning for serious off-label promotion), Dova has no contractual leverage to require stricter measures (e.g., removal from Product promotion, termination) to protect itself from regulatory action.
findings.remediation: Add language requiring Valeant to consult with Dova on appropriate remedial actions for material violations and to give good faith consideration to Dova's recommendations. For serious violations (e.g., off-label promotion, kickbacks), require immediate removal of the personnel from Product promotion pending investigation.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information relating to the sale, commercialization, marketing and promotion of the Product, as may be mutually agreed by the Parties from time to time...
findings.description: Data sharing is entirely discretionary ('mutually agreed'), potentially hindering Valeant's ability to perform co-promotion activities, but more critically, the clause lacks data security and confidentiality specifications.
findings.reasoning: While the discretionary nature favors Dova, the lack of specified data security standards, confidentiality obligations, or use restrictions (beyond 'in connection with the Valeant Activities') creates risk that Valeant could mishandle sensitive data (including account-level information and [***] redacted data), potentially exposing Dova to data breach liability or HIPAA violations if the data includes patient information.
findings.remediation: Add specific data security standards (e.g., encryption, access controls), confidentiality obligations, permitted use restrictions, and a requirement for Valeant to indemnify Dova for data breaches caused by Valeant's mishandling.

findings.description: Missing clause text prevents verification of cure period for material breach termination rights
findings.reasoning: Section 12.2 is cross-referenced in Section 4.3.6 regarding termination provisions, specifically to verify the existence of a cure period for material breaches. The absence of the actual clause text creates a critical gap in due diligence, preventing confirmation of whether Dova has standard protections against immediate termination. Without a cure period, Valeant could theoretically terminate the co-promotion agreement immediately upon alleging a material breach, exposing Dova to sudden loss of commercialization rights and revenue without opportunity to remedy the alleged breach. This is particularly acute given Valeant's role as co-promotion partner with operational control under Section 4 references.
findings.remediation: Immediately request the complete text of Section 12.2 from counterparty. Verify inclusion of: (1) explicit cure period of not less than 30 days (60 days for payment breaches) for material breaches; (2) written notice specifying the breach in reasonable detail; (3) opportunity to dispute the existence of a material breach prior to termination; and (4) automatic stay of termination if cure is commenced within the period and diligently pursued. If cure period is absent, negotiate insertion of standard cure period language. If Valeant refuses, consider requiring arbitration or judicial determination of material breach before termination takes effect.

findings.clause_text: [CLAUSE TEXT NOT PROVIDED - Referenced in Section 4.3.11 regarding dispute resolution timeline and scope but full text unavailable for analysis]
findings.description: Material gap in due diligence: Dispute resolution clause (Section 13.6) text is missing, preventing assessment of timeline obligations and scope referenced in Section 4.3.11
findings.reasoning: Section 13.6 contains the dispute resolution process referenced in Section 4.3.11. Without the actual text, it is impossible to verify critical parameters including: (1) whether the timeline for dispute escalation creates operational bottlenecks or statutory limitations risks; (2) whether the scope includes mandatory arbitration that might limit Dova's ability to seek injunctive relief for IP violations or terminate the co-promotion arrangement; (3) venue and governing law provisions that may expose Dova to unfavorable jurisdictions. In co-promotion agreements, dispute resolution mechanisms directly impact the ability to protect product IP and exit unprofitable arrangements.
