The absence of this text represents a critical due diligence failure that prevents proper risk assessment.
findings.remediation: 1. IMMEDIATE: Obtain complete text of Section 13.6 from counterparty or contract repository before proceeding with agreement execution. 2. Upon receipt, verify that Section 4.3.11's reference to Section 13.6 does not create timeline conflicts (e.g., short cure periods vs. long escalation periods). 3. Ensure Section 13.6 preserves Dova's right to seek preliminary injunctive relief in court for IP breaches despite any mandatory arbitration clause. 4. Confirm governing law and venue are neutral or favorable to Dova. 5. If Section 13.6 contains unfavorable binding arbitration or lengthy dispute timelines, negotiate amendment to allow expedited resolution for IP disputes and termination disputes.

findings.clause_ref: Definition of 'Detailing' (Critical to scope of Sections 4.3.10 and 4.5.3)
findings.description: Missing definition of critical operational term 'Detailing' which governs scope of co-promotion obligations in Sections 4.3.10 and 4.5.3
findings.reasoning: The section intended to define 'Detailing' contains no text, yet the title indicates this definition is critical to the scope of Sections 4.3.10 and 4.5.3. Without a defined scope of Detailing activities, Dova cannot ascertain the extent of Valeant's promotional obligations, the boundaries of permitted detailing activities, minimum performance standards, or excluded activities. This creates severe ambiguity regarding contractual performance obligations and could lead to disputes over whether Valeant has met its co-promotion duties or exceeded its authority. Cross-references indicate the definition may exist in Section 1.14, but its absence here creates immediate interpretive risk for operational compliance.

findings.clause_text: "Confidential Information" shall mean all secret, confidential, non-public or proprietary Know-How, whether provided in written, oral, graphic, video, computer or other form, provided by or on behalf of one Party to the other Party pursuant to this Agreement...

This exposes the recipient to breach claims even for legitimately obtained information.
findings.remediation: Add standard exclusions: 'Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no breach of this Agreement; (b) was rightfully in Recipient's possession prior to disclosure; (c) is rightfully disclosed to Recipient by a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed by Recipient without use of or reference to Discloser's Confidential Information.'

findings.clause_text: Valeant agrees to assign, and hereby does assign... any and all right, title and interest that Valeant (or any such Affiliates, employees or other representatives) may have in or to any Invention
findings.description: Absence of affirmative disclosure duty requiring Valeant to identify and report inventions to Dova
findings.reasoning: While Valeant is obligated to assign rights, the clause contains no duty to disclose inventions when they are conceived or reduced to practice. This allows Valeant to conceal inventions, exploit them for competing products, or delay disclosure until statutory patent bars expire. Dova cannot enforce assignment rights over unknown IP, effectively rendering the assignment provision unenforceable in practice and risking loss of patent rights.
findings.remediation: Add explicit invention disclosure obligations requiring Valeant to promptly notify Dova in writing of any potentially assignable inventions within 30 days of conception or reduction to practice, with detailed descriptions and supporting documentation sufficient to assess ownership and enable patent filing.

findings.clause_text: shall cause its Affiliates and its and their respective employees and other representatives to assign to Dova
findings.description: Lack of enforcement mechanism or cooperation obligations for securing employee assignments
findings.reasoning: The obligation to 'cause' employees to assign lacks specific mechanisms if employees refuse. Dova lacks contractual privity with Valeant's employees. Without further assurances, escalation procedures, or specific cooperation mandates, Dova may be unable to perfect legal title to critical inventions if individual inventors contest the assignment or demand compensation.
findings.remediation: Add specific obligations requiring Valeant to: (i) maintain signed pre-invention assignment agreements from all employees and contractors working on the Product, (ii) deliver executed copies to Dova upon request, (iii) provide reasonable assistance in executing patent assignments or other documents, and (iv) indemnify Dova for losses arising from employee refusal to assign or claims of compensation.

findings.clause_text: For clarity, any and all Inventions and any information contained therein or related thereto shall constitute Confidential Information of Dova
findings.description: Overbroad classification of all Inventions as Confidential Information creates enforceability and practical conflicts
findings.reasoning: Declaring all Inventions, without limitation, as Dova's Confidential Information may be challenged as an unreasonable restraint on Valeant's ability to use general skills and know-how post-termination. Some jurisdictions may invalidate this as exceeding legitimate trade secret protection. Additionally, this conflicts with patent prosecution if Dova files patents (public disclosure) while simultaneously claiming the invention remains confidential.
findings.remediation: Qualify that only proprietary aspects of Inventions constitute Confidential Information, explicitly permit Valeant to use general skills, knowledge, and publicly available information learned during engagement, and add exception for information disclosed in patent applications or required by regulatory authorities.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall have and retain sole and exclusive right, title and interest in and to all inventions... made... by Valeant... to the extent primarily related to the Product
findings.description: No carve-out for Valeant Background IP or joint invention mechanisms
findings.reasoning: If Valeant incorporates its pre-existing trade secrets or background IP into Product improvements, or if Valeant independently develops patentable contributions using its own resources while 'performing activities,' the clause claims sole Dova ownership. However, courts may find joint ownership or implied licenses in favor of Valeant, clouding Dova's title. This also risks Valeant refusing to contribute improvements if it loses rights to its own background technology.
findings.remediation: Explicitly exclude Valeant's Background IP from assignment. Add provisions addressing joint inventions: if Valeant contributes independent IP not derived from Dova's Confidential Information, Dova receives exclusive ownership (or exclusive license) for the Product field, with Valeant retaining ownership for other fields, and mutual cross-licensing for improvements.

findings.clause_text: [SECTION NOT PROVIDED - REFERENCED ONLY]

This gap exposes Dova to potential over-promotion obligations, Valeant encroachment on Dova's other products, and disputes over whether activities are 'primarily related' to the undefined Product. The 'primarily related' qualifier without a defined Product creates unlimited interpretive discretion favoring Valeant.

Without this definition, Dova cannot limit liability for unauthorized statements, off-label promotion, or data breaches by Valeant's sales force, contractors, or downstream subcontractors. This creates joint and several liability exposure under FDA regulations and state consumer protection laws.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive definition: 'Representatives means a Party's employees, officers, directors, and specifically identified contractors who: (i) are authorized in writing by such Party to perform activities under this Agreement; (ii) have executed confidentiality and compliance obligations no less protective than Article [X]; and (iii) have completed training on applicable laws and the Product's approved labeling. Excludes any subcontractor, distributor, or third party unless specifically approved in writing by the other Party.' Additionally, negotiate mutual indemnification for acts/omissions of each party's respective Representatives.

findings.clause_text: Valeant agrees to assign, and hereby does assign, to Dova (and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their respective employees and other representatives to assign to Dova) any and all right, title and interest that Valeant (or any such Affiliates, employees or other representatives) may have in or to any Invention
findings.description: Immediate irrevocable assignment of IP rights without warranty of title or indemnification against third-party claims
findings.reasoning: The 'hereby does assign' language effects an immediate, irrevocable transfer of ownership rights, yet the clause contains no warranty that Valeant actually possesses valid, unencumbered title to these inventions. If third parties (such as former employers of Valeant's employees, academic institutions, or joint inventors not party to this Agreement) assert ownership claims against the assigned inventions, Dova assumes all litigation risk and defense costs without recourse against Valeant. This creates unlimited liability exposure for Dova regarding the validity of title transferred.
findings.remediation: Add explicit warranties that (a) Valeant has good and marketable title to all assigned Inventions free from any liens or encumbrances, (b) the assignments do not violate any third-party rights, and (c) Valeant has obtained valid assignment agreements from all employees and representatives. Add indemnification requiring Valeant to defend and hold harmless Dova from third-party ownership claims or challenges to title.

(iii) made, discovered, conceived, reduced to practice or generated by Valeant (or its employees or representatives) in performing its activities pursuant to this Agreement to the extent primarily related to the Product...
findings.description: Overbroad capture of Valeant's general business improvements and background IP without carve-out
findings.reasoning: The clause captures 'improvements... relating to the Product' conceived by Valeant during the Term. This could be interpreted to capture Valeant's independent improvements to its own background technology, manufacturing processes, or general pharmaceutical know-how if such improvements can be argued to 'relate to' the Product or be 'primarily related' to it. The subjective standard 'primarily related' provides no objective boundary, potentially stripping Valeant of its general business improvements and creating disputes over whether improvements to Valeant's proprietary delivery systems or formulations constitute 'improvements' to the Product.

Limit assignment to inventions that specifically incorporate Dova's Confidential Information or are solely and specifically developed for the Product (not general business improvements).

findings.clause_text: For clarity, any and all Inventions and any information contained therein or related thereto shall constitute Confidential Information of Dova.
findings.description: Perpetual confidentiality classification without standard exceptions or temporal limitations
findings.reasoning: The clause unilaterally declares all Inventions and related information to be Dova's Confidential Information without the standard exceptions found in confidentiality provisions (e.g., information already known to Valeant, publicly available information, information received from third parties without restriction, or information independently developed). This creates perpetual confidentiality obligations that could prevent Valeant from using its own general knowledge or publicly available information. It also creates enforcement conflicts if the 'Inventions' include information that later becomes public through independent means.
findings.remediation: Add standard confidentiality exceptions: (a) information already in Valeant's possession without confidentiality obligations, (b) information that becomes public through no fault of Valeant, (c) information received from third parties without restriction, and (d) information independently developed by Valeant without use of Dova's Confidential Information. Specify that confidentiality obligations survive termination for a defined period (e.g., 5 years) or, for trade secrets, until public.

findings.clause_text: Valeant agrees to assign, and hereby does assign, to Dova (and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their respective employees and other representatives to assign to Dova)...

However, Valeant may lack contractual privity with certain representatives (such as independent contractors, clinical investigators, or CROs) to enforce this obligation. Without a requirement that Valeant obtain written IP assignments from all representatives before they begin work, or a mechanism to ensure representatives are bound, Valeant faces breach risk if a third-party representative refuses to assign, and Dova risks not receiving valid title.

Add a representation that all representatives are under written obligation to assign IP.

findings.clause_text: ...made, discovered, conceived, reduced to practice or generated by Valeant (or its employees or representatives) in performing its activities pursuant to this Agreement to the extent primarily related to the Product...

It also lacks a 'halo period' (e.g., 6-12 months post-termination) for inventions conceived during the Term but filed thereafter, which is standard in R&D collaborations to prevent premature termination to avoid assignment obligations.

Pay particular attention to redacted provisions in Articles dealing with: (a) financial terms (royalties, milestones), (b) performance metrics and minimum obligations, (c) termination for convenience provisions, and (d) liability limitations. findings.clause_text: WHEREAS, the Parties believe that it would be mutually beneficial to collaborate on promotional activities for the Product and, accordingly, Dova desires that Valeant conduct certain promotional activities, and Valeant desires to conduct such activities, for the Product in the Territory;
findings.description: Recitals use precatory 'desires' language regarding Valeant's promotional obligations rather than mandatory terms, creating interpretive ambiguity if operative provisions are not sufficiently specific
findings.reasoning: The recitals state that Dova 'desires' Valeant to conduct activities and Valeant 'desires' to conduct them. This precatory language suggests mutual aspiration rather than binding obligation. While the recitals are followed by 'NOW, THEREFORE' indicating operative provisions follow (not provided in this excerpt), if the operative provisions in Article 2 (or the applicable performance section) do not use mandatory language ('shall,' 'must') or fail to specify concrete performance metrics (call volumes, detailing frequency, FTE commitments), a court could interpret Valeant's obligations as merely discretionary based on these recitals. This creates enforcement risk regarding Valeant's promotional duties, which are the core consideration for Dova in this co-promotion arrangement.
findings.remediation: Ensure that the operative provisions of the Agreement (likely Article 2 or a 'Duties and Responsibilities' section) contain mandatory, specific language regarding Valeant's promotional obligations, including: (a) minimum detailing requirements or call volume commitments, (b) field force sizing (FTEs), (c) specific promotional materials approval rights, and (d) performance metrics with cure periods. Consider adding a non-reliance clause or explicit statement that recitals are not operative provisions, or alternatively, ensure recitals accurately reflect the binding obligations in the operative sections.

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No governing law or jurisdiction clause identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of governing law clause creates jurisdictional uncertainty and exposes Dova to potentially unfavorable application of foreign state laws without predictable contract interpretation rules.
findings.reasoning: Without explicit governing law selection, courts will apply conflict of laws principles that may result in application of Valeant's home jurisdiction law (potentially Delaware or another state with unpredictable pharmaceutical regulatory precedents) rather than Dova's preferred jurisdiction. This creates uncertainty regarding interpretation of regulatory compliance obligations, promotional restrictions, and intellectual property rights. In pharmaceutical co-promotion, where FDA regulations and state consumer protection laws vary significantly, lack of governing law exposes Dova to unexpected statutory interpretations regarding off-label promotion, anti-kickback statutes, and product liability allocation.
findings.remediation: Insert explicit governing law clause specifying Delaware law (or Dova's preferred jurisdiction) applies to the agreement, excluding conflict of laws principles. Include carve-out for mandatory FDA regulations and applicable state consumer protection laws that cannot be contracted away. Specify exclusive jurisdiction in Delaware courts (or preferred forum) with mutual waiver of objections to venue. Consider adding arbitration provision for commercial disputes while preserving court jurisdiction for IP and regulatory injunctive relief.

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No indemnification provisions identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of indemnification clauses exposes Dova to unlimited liability for Valeant's promotional activities, regulatory violations, product liability claims, and third-party intellectual property infringement arising from co-promotion efforts.
findings.reasoning: Pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements require precise liability allocation because: (1) Valeant's sales force will promote Dova's product, creating potential for off-label promotion claims, anti-kickback violations, and misrepresentation liability; (2) Product liability claims may allege failure to warn or inadequate labeling based on promotional materials created by Valeant; (3) Third-party IP claims may arise from Valeant's marketing materials. Without indemnification, Dova bears full responsibility for Valeant's regulatory compliance failures, sales force misconduct, and promotional content errors. This is particularly dangerous given Valeant's operational history and the high-stakes regulatory environment for pharmaceuticals (potential FDA fines exceeding millions, DOJ enforcement actions, and class action liability).
findings.remediation: Negotiate comprehensive mutual indemnification including: (a) Dova indemnifies for product liability (manufacturing defects, product safety, regulatory approval of drug itself), IP infringement by the drug compound, and Dova's breach of regulatory warranties; (b) Valeant indemnifies for promotional activities (all claims arising from sales force conduct, marketing materials, off-label promotion allegations, anti-kickback violations), IP infringement in marketing materials created by Valeant, and Valeant's data privacy breaches; (c) Mutual indemnification for general breaches, confidentiality violations, and IP infringement; (d) Carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and regulatory fines where both parties contributed; (e) Control of defense provisions requiring Valeant to defend Dova against promotion-related claims using counsel acceptable to Dova; (f) Survival of indemnification obligations for statute of limitations period applicable to underlying claims (typically 6+ years for product liability).

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No limitation of liability provisions identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of liability caps exposes Dova to unlimited damages for breaches, including consequential, indirect, and punitive damages, creating catastrophic financial exposure in a high-risk pharmaceutical arrangement.
findings.reasoning: Pharmaceutical agreements carry unique risks requiring liability limitations: (1) Product liability exposure can reach billions in class action scenarios; (2) Regulatory violations carry statutory penalties (False Claims Act treble damages, FDA consent decree costs); (3) Market withdrawal costs (recalls, inventory destruction) can exceed hundreds of millions; (4) Data breaches involving patient health information trigger HIPAA penalties and state notification costs. Without liability caps, a single breach by Dova (e.g., supply interruption, data breach, or IP infringement claim) could result in damages exceeding the entire value of the co-promotion arrangement and threaten Dova's solvency. The absence of consequential damages exclusions is particularly problematic because Valeant could claim lost profits from failed product launches, market share losses, and reputational harm that are difficult to quantify and disproportionate to actual breach severity.
findings.remediation: Insert mutual limitation of liability clause: (a) Cap direct damages at the greater of $[X] million or fees paid in preceding 12 months (suggest $10-50M minimum given pharma risk profile); (b) Exclude consequential, indirect, incidental, special, and punitive damages entirely; (c) Critical carve-outs preserving unlimited liability for: (i) breaches of confidentiality/data security (HIPAA/patient data), (ii) IP infringement and misappropriation, (iii) indemnification obligations (particularly product liability), (iv) gross negligence, willful misconduct, and regulatory violations, (v) payment obligations, (vi) essential remedies (injunctive relief); (d) Ensure cap applies per claim and aggregate; (e) Clarify that insurance proceeds do not reduce liability caps.

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No insurance requirements identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of insurance requirements leaves Dova without assurance that Valeant maintains adequate coverage for product liability, professional liability, and general commercial risks, creating unfunded liability exposure.
findings.reasoning: Pharmaceutical co-promotion requires substantial insurance backing because: (1) Product liability claims often involve multiple parties with joint and several liability; (2) Professional liability covers regulatory compliance failures and promotional errors; (3) General liability covers premises and operations; (4) Cyber liability covers patient data breaches. Without contractual insurance requirements, Valeant could operate with minimal coverage or allow policies to lapse, leaving Dova solely responsible for defense costs and settlements when claims arise from Valeant's promotional activities. The absence of additional insured status for Dova is particularly problematic because Dova cannot access Valeant's coverage directly for claims arising from Valeant's conduct.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive insurance requirements: (a) Commercial General Liability ($5M per occurrence/$10M aggregate); (b) Product Liability ($10M per occurrence/$20M aggregate); (c) Professional Liability/E&O ($5M) covering regulatory compliance and promotional activities; (d) Cyber Liability ($5M) covering patient health information; (e) Workers Compensation (statutory); (f) Dova named as additional insured on CGL, Product Liability, and Cyber policies with primary and non-contributory status; (g) 30-day written notice of cancellation or material change; (h) Certificates of insurance provided annually and upon request; (i) Self-insurance only acceptable with A.M. Best A- rating or better and Dova approval.

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No dispute resolution mechanism identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of dispute resolution provisions exposes Dova to immediate litigation in potentially unfavorable forums without mandatory negotiation or mediation requirements that could preserve the commercial relationship and reduce costs.
findings.reasoning: Without structured dispute resolution, Valeant could immediately file suit in any jurisdiction with proper venue, potentially selecting a forum inconvenient to Dova or with unpredictable pharmaceutical precedent. The absence of mandatory negotiation and mediation eliminates opportunities for business-level resolution of disputes regarding promotional efforts, market share allocations, or regulatory compliance before incurring litigation costs. For pharmaceutical agreements, public litigation risks disclosure of confidential drug development data, regulatory strategies, and pricing information through discovery and public filings. The lack of arbitration provisions also means no ability to select pharma-experienced decision-makers or maintain confidentiality.
findings.remediation: Insert tiered dispute resolution clause: (a) Mandatory good faith negotiation between designated executives (VP-level or above) for 30 days; (b) Non-binding mediation administered by AAA or JAMS in a mutually agreeable neutral location (or split costs) for 60 days; (c) Binding arbitration (for commercial disputes - payment, performance) or litigation (for IP, regulatory, or injunctive relief) in [Dova's preferred forum, e.g., Delaware or NC]; (d) Confidentiality of proceedings; (e) Allocation of costs (loser pays or each bears own); (f) Preservation of right to seek preliminary injunctive relief in court for IP breaches or regulatory emergencies; (g) Governing law selection consistent with Section 13 governing law provision.

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No assignment or change of control provisions identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of assignment restrictions allows Valeant to transfer obligations to competitors or entities with inadequate regulatory compliance infrastructure without Dova's consent, creating regulatory and competitive risks.
findings.reasoning: Pharmaceutical co-promotion partners must maintain specific regulatory qualifications (FDA compliance history, sales force training, adverse event reporting capabilities). Without assignment restrictions, Valeant could transfer the agreement to a competitor of Dova or an entity lacking adequate compliance infrastructure through M&A (change of control) or assignment. This exposes Dova to: (1) Regulatory risk if the assignee lacks FDA compliance capabilities; (2) Competitive risk if the assignee is a competitor; (3) Credit risk if the assignee lacks financial stability. Standard assignment clauses prevent these risks by requiring consent for transfers.
findings.remediation: Insert assignment and change of control clause: (a) Neither party may assign without prior written consent of the other (not unreasonably withheld for affiliates with equal creditworthiness); (b) Change of control (sale of >50% of voting stock, merger, or sale of substantially all assets) constitutes assignment requiring consent; (c) Dova may withhold consent if assignee: (i) is a competitor in the therapeutic area, (ii) lacks FDA promotional compliance certification, (iii) has adverse regulatory enforcement history, or (iv) fails to meet financial stability standards; (d) Assignment does not relieve assignor of liability unless Dova expressly releases in writing; (e) Exceptions for internal reorganizations with 30-day notice; (f) Dova may terminate for cause if assignment occurs without consent.

findings.clause_text: [MISSING - No survival clause identified in Sections 13.1-13.17]
findings.description: Absence of survival provisions creates uncertainty regarding post-termination obligations for confidentiality, indemnification, payment obligations, and IP rights, potentially allowing early termination of critical protections.
findings.reasoning: Pharmaceutical agreements generate long-tail liabilities: product liability claims may arise years after termination; patient data confidentiality obligations persist indefinitely under HIPAA; payment obligations for royalties or milestones may survive termination; trade secrets require perpetual protection. Without explicit survival language, a party could argue that confidentiality, indemnification, and IP obligations terminated with the agreement, exposing Dova to: (1) Loss of indemnification for product liability claims arising post-termination; (2) Loss of confidentiality protections for trade secrets; (3) Uncertainty regarding payment of accrued royalties. While some obligations survive by operation of law, explicit language prevents litigation over scope.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive survival clause specifying that the following survive termination: (a) Confidentiality obligations regarding patient data and personal information (perpetual or as required by HIPAA); (b) Confidentiality of trade secrets (perpetual); (c) General confidentiality (3-5 years post-termination); (d) Indemnification obligations (perpetual for product liability, 3 years for other claims); (e) Payment obligations (until paid in full); (f) IP ownership and license grants (perpetual for surviving licenses); (g) Dispute resolution procedures; (h) Limitations of liability; (i) Survival clause itself. Specify survival periods run from date of termination, not contract execution.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall not be required to use any Product Materials that have not been approved by Valeant or which have not incorporated comments provided by Valeant and nothing herein shall require Valeant to use all Product Materials created or prepared by Dova and Valeant reserves the right not to use certain Product Materials.
findings.description: Valeant retains absolute discretion to reject Product Materials without objective standards or good faith requirements
findings.reasoning: This language allows Valeant to unilaterally block co-promotion activities by rejecting materials without cause, even if such materials are compliant with regulatory requirements and Dova's medical/legal review. The absence of a 'not to be unreasonably withheld' standard or objective rejection criteria creates strategic exposure for Dova.
findings.remediation: Insert 'not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed' after 'approved by Valeant' and specify that Valeant must provide written reasons for rejection citing specific regulatory or legal deficiencies.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall be solely responsible for ensuring that the Product Materials prepared and approved by it are in compliance with the Regulatory Approval for the Product, the Product Labeling and Applicable Law.
findings.description: Absolute compliance liability without carve-out for Valeant misuse or unauthorized modifications
findings.reasoning: While Dova controls content creation, Valeant's Field Force Personnel ultimately use these materials. The 'solely responsible' language exposes Dova to regulatory liability and penalties even if non-compliance results from Valeant's unauthorized modifications, off-label promotion, or failure to follow approved materials. No indemnification or shared liability mechanism is present.
findings.remediation: Add carve-out: 'provided that Dova shall not be responsible for non-compliance resulting from unauthorized modifications by Valeant or Field Force Personnel or use of Product Materials in a manner inconsistent with Dova's written instructions or the approved Product Labeling.'

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall have the right, but not the obligation, to conduct such additional training itself, provided that the Valeant trainers have been trained by Dova, and provided further that Dova shall have the right to attend such training upon reasonable notice by Valeant to Dova.
findings.description: Valeant may conduct unsupervised training without Dova approval of content or materials
findings.reasoning: Valeant can conduct additional training using its own personnel who have merely been 'trained by Dova' (attended Dova's training). This creates significant regulatory risk as Valeant could train Field Force Personnel on off-label uses, unsubstantiated claims, or non-compliant messaging. Dova's only remedy is the right to attend; there is no right to approve content, stop non-compliant training, or require Valeant to use Dova-approved materials.
findings.remediation: Add requirement that 'Dova must approve in writing all training content, materials, and messaging prior to such additional training, and Dova may prohibit any training that deviates from approved Product Labeling or Applicable Law.'

findings.clause_text: [General section reference - no specific cap language present in Section 4.4.1]
findings.description: No limitation of liability for breaches of materials preparation, approval, or training obligations
findings.reasoning: Section 4.4.1 imposes extensive obligations on Dova regarding regulatory compliance of materials and training. The absence of any liability cap in this Section (or reference to a general liability cap in the Agreement) exposes Dova to unlimited damages for breaches, including consequential damages, regulatory fines, and third-party claims arising from materials or training activities.
findings.remediation: Add: 'Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, Dova's total liability for breaches of this Section 4.4.1 shall be limited to [twelve (12) months] of fees paid under this Agreement, except for breaches of Applicable Law or regulatory requirements which shall be subject to a cap of [insert higher amount or mutual indemnification].'

findings.clause_text: provide verbal feedback to Dova in advance of the Valeant Activates to allow for Valeant to review such content and provide verbal feedback to Dova in advance of use of the Product Materials. Within [***] of receipt of such Product Materials, Valeant shall verbally provide to Dova any comments and/or proposed revisions to such Product Materials
findings.description: Mandatory verbal feedback creates documentation gaps and evidentiary risks
findings.reasoning: The requirement for 'verbal' feedback rather than written comments creates no audit trail. In disputes regarding whether Valeant provided timely feedback or whether Dova reasonably considered suggestions, neither party will have documentary evidence. This undermines Dova's ability to prove it complied with consultation obligations and Valeant's ability to prove it objected to non-compliant materials.
findings.remediation: Replace 'verbally provide' with 'provide in writing (which may include email)' and require written confirmation of receipt and consideration.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall prepare and control the content of (i) all Product training materials for Field Force Personnel (the 'Product Training Materials') and (ii) all Product marketing and educational materials (the 'Promotional Materials')
findings.description: Ambiguous IP ownership and rights in derivative works
findings.reasoning: While Dova 'prepares and controls' content, the Agreement does not explicitly assign ownership of intellectual property rights in the Product Materials to Dova. Valeant provides comments and revisions which Dova may incorporate. Without explicit assignment, Valeant could claim joint ownership or rights in the 'comments' it provides, potentially restricting Dova's ability to use modified materials with other partners or claiming rights to derivative works.
findings.remediation: Add explicit language: 'Dova shall own all right, title, and interest in and to all Product Materials, including all modifications and derivative works. Valeant hereby assigns to Dova all rights in any comments, suggestions, or revisions provided by Valeant.'

findings.clause_text: In the event that Dova incurs costs and expenses for which Valeant is responsible under this Section 4.4.1, Dova may deduct such amounts from the payments due under Section 6.3 and shall include a description thereof in the applicable report under Section 6.3.
findings.description: Unilateral set-off right lacks procedural safeguards
findings.reasoning: While the set-off right favors Dova, the absence of prior notice or dispute resolution mechanism creates procedural risk. If Valeant disputes the amount deducted, the unilateral action could be challenged as a breach of payment obligations. The 'description' requirement is vague regarding required detail.
findings.remediation: Add: 'Dova shall provide fifteen (15) days prior written notice of intent to deduct, including detailed documentation of such costs. Valeant may dispute such costs in good faith, and Dova shall not deduct disputed amounts until resolution.'

findings.clause_text: [No indemnification language present in section]
findings.description: Absence of indemnification for IP infringement and regulatory violations
findings.reasoning: Section imposes obligations regarding materials creation and training but contains no indemnification provisions. If Product Materials infringe third-party IP, or if training activities violate regulatory requirements, there is no allocation of indemnification risk. Dova could face claims for materials it created, while Valeant could face claims for how it used them, with no mutual protection.
findings.remediation: Add mutual indemnification: Dova indemnifies Valeant for IP infringement in materials created by Dova; Valeant indemnifies Dova for unauthorized modifications to materials and for regulatory violations arising from Valeant's training or use of materials.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall have the responsibility for on-going training of its Field Force Personnel engaged in Detailing in accordance with customary practice in the pharmaceutical industry.

findings.remediation: Replace with specific requirements: 'Valeant shall conduct ongoing training at least quarterly, consistent with PhRMA Code and OIG compliance guidance, and shall provide Dova with certificates of completion.'

findings.clause_text: Valeant will certify in writing to Dova that all Field Force Personnel have completed the training described in this Section 4.4.1(b).

findings.clause_text: [Text not provided in analysis input; section referenced as 'payment terms referenced for set-off']
findings.description: Unverified set-off provisions create risk of unilateral deduction rights by Valeant from royalties and co-promotion payments owed to Dova, potentially permitting set-off for disputed amounts, cross-affiliate obligations, or unrelated debts without notice or limitation.
findings.reasoning: In co-promotion agreements with larger pharmaceutical entities like Valeant, payment sections typically grant the larger party broad rights to set-off amounts owed to the smaller party against any alleged debts, disputes, or affiliate obligations. Without visibility into Section 6.3's actual language, we must assume Valeant may withhold substantial royalty payments citing unrelated disputes, creating severe cash flow disruption for Dova and forcing Dova to litigate for recovery. The lack of specific text regarding whether set-off is limited to undisputed, matured debts between the specific contracting parties (excluding affiliates) creates unacceptable uncertainty in a high-value pharmaceutical co-promotion.

Negotiate to: (1) Limit set-off rights to undisputed, matured monetary obligations solely between Dova Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and Valeant Pharmaceuticals North America LLC (explicitly excluding affiliates and parent/subsidiary entities); (2) Require 30 days prior written notice of any intended set-off with opportunity to cure or dispute the underlying obligation; (3) Cap set-off amounts to the specific disputed amount, not the entire payment obligation or future royalties; (4) Ensure mutuality of set-off rights permitting Dova to exercise identical rights against Valeant; (5) Explicitly exclude set-off for amounts subject to good faith dispute pending resolution through the dispute resolution mechanism.

findings.reasoning: The contract contains compliance obligations that reference 'Code' (likely referring to the PhRMA Code, FDA regulations, or other industry code of conduct), but the term is not defined anywhere in the agreement. This creates significant ambiguity regarding the scope of compliance obligations, potential regulatory exposure, and dispute risk. For a co-promotion agreement involving pharmaceutical products (Dova's products promoted by Valeant), undefined 'Code' references could impose unknown compliance burdens, particularly around promotional materials, speaker programs, and HCP interactions. The parties may have materially different understandings of which code(s) apply (PhRMA Code? IFPMA? Local state codes? FDA promotional guidelines?), leading to inconsistent compliance practices and potential FDA enforcement action or False Claims Act exposure.
findings.remediation: Negotiate explicit definition of 'Code' including: (1) specific identification of applicable codes (e.g., 'PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals, as amended from time to time'); (2) whether FDA regulations and OPDP guidance are incorporated by reference; (3) handling of future amendments to referenced codes; (4) geographic scope (US-only or international); and (5) dispute resolution mechanism if codes conflict. Consider adding schedule listing all applicable codes and regulations. For Dova as product owner, ensure definition preserves right to enforce stricter internal standards without triggering breach claims from Valeant.

findings.clause_ref: Definition of 'Applicable Law' (scope of compliance obligations)
findings.description: The definition of 'Applicable Law' is entirely absent, leaving compliance obligations undefined in a highly regulated pharmaceutical co-promotion arrangement involving FDA-regulated promotional activities.
findings.reasoning: In pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements between a product owner (Dova) and co-promotion partner (Valeant), 'Applicable Law' must encompass FDA regulations (21 CFR, OPDP promotional guidelines), healthcare fraud and abuse laws (Anti-Kickback Statute, False Claims Act), data privacy requirements (HIPAA), and state pharmacy laws. Without this definition: (1) parties may have conflicting interpretations of compliance obligations leading to regulatory violations; (2) indemnification triggers become ambiguous regarding which violations are covered; (3) insurance coverage may be disputed for undefined regulatory risks; (4) criminal and civil exposure for promotional misconduct is unallocated. This is particularly critical given Valeant's history of regulatory scrutiny and the high-risk nature of co-promotional activities.
findings.remediation: Insert a comprehensive definition of 'Applicable Law' that explicitly includes: (1) all applicable federal, state, local, and foreign laws, statutes, regulations, and ordinances; (2) specific reference to FDA regulations (21 CFR Parts 201, 202, 312, 314), OPDP guidelines, and FDA guidance documents on promotional materials; (3) healthcare fraud and abuse laws including the federal Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b), False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733), and analogous state laws; (4) data privacy and security laws including HIPAA (45 CFR Parts 160, 164), state data breach notification laws, and international data protection regulations if applicable; (5) industry codes including the PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals; (6) all applicable manufacturing and quality standards (cGMP). Ensure the definition is broad enough to capture evolving regulations but specific enough to provide clear compliance guidance.

findings.clause_text: In the event that Dova incurs costs and expenses for which Valeant is responsible under this Section 4.4.1, Dova may deduct such amounts from the payments due under Section 6.3 and shall include a description thereof in the applicable report under Section 6.3.
findings.description: Unilateral set-off right lacking procedural safeguards, notice requirements, or dispute resolution mechanisms
findings.reasoning: Dova can unilaterally deduct disputed amounts from payments due to Valeant (likely co-promotion fees under Section 6.3) without prior notice, opportunity to contest, or limitation on the percentage deductible. This creates cash flow disruption and accounting disputes, particularly since the description in a 'report' may not provide adequate detail to verify the deduction.
findings.remediation: Negotiate protections requiring (i) written notice 30 days prior to deduction, (ii) limitation to undisputed amounts or final judgments, (iii) right to dispute via expedited arbitration before withholding, and (iv) cap on percentage of any payment that may be deducted (e.g., 10-20%).

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall verbally provide to Dova any comments and/or proposed revisions to such Product Materials
findings.description: Mandatory verbal feedback creates documentation gaps and evidentiary risks
findings.reasoning: Requiring 'verbal' feedback rather than written comments eliminates the paper trail necessary to prove (1) whether Valeant provided timely feedback, (2) the substance of suggestions to determine if Dova 'reasonably considered' them, and (3) whether feedback was incorporated. This undermines contractual enforcement and dispute resolution.
findings.remediation: Amend to require written feedback (email acceptable) within the specified timeframe, with clear identification of which comments must be incorporated to secure Valeant's approval rights.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall be solely responsible for ensuring that the Product Materials prepared and approved by it are in compliance with the Regulatory Approval for the Product, the Product Labeling and Applicable Law.
findings.description: Absolute compliance liability on Dova without carve-out for Valeant misuse, unauthorized modifications, or failure to train
findings.reasoning: Despite Valeant's right to reject materials and the risk of unauthorized modifications by Field Force Personnel (prohibited but not prevented), Dova retains sole responsibility for compliance. There is no exception for liability arising from Valeant's unauthorized changes, use of materials by untrained personnel, or deviation from approved content during Detailing activities.
findings.remediation: Add carve-out stating Dova is not responsible for compliance violations directly caused by Valeant's (i) unauthorized modifications to Product Materials, (ii) use of materials by Field Force Personnel who have not completed required training, or (iii) failure to comply with Dova's written instructions regarding use.

findings.clause_text: Valeant reserves the right not to use certain Product Materials
findings.description: Absolute discretion to reject materials without good faith standard, objective criteria, or deemed approval mechanism
findings.reasoning: Valeant may withhold approval or refuse to use materials without any requirement to act reasonably, in good faith, or within a specified timeframe. This creates risk of strategic delay or unreasonable rejection to avoid performance obligations or force renegotiation, with no recourse for Dova.
findings.remediation: Add requirement that Valeant's approval rights must be exercised reasonably and not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, with a 'deemed approved' clause if Valeant fails to object within [10] business days after the feedback period.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall prepare and control the content of (i) all Product Training Materials... and (ii) all Product marketing and educational materials... Valeant shall use only Product Materials approved by Dova...
findings.description: Ambiguous IP ownership and lack of explicit license grant to Valeant
findings.reasoning: While Dova 'prepares and controls' content, the agreement does not explicitly (1) assign ownership of all IP rights in Product Materials to Dova, (2) grant Valeant a license to use the materials, or (3) address ownership of derivative works incorporating Valeant's suggestions. This creates infringement risk and uncertainty regarding Valeant's rights to use materials post-termination or in the field.
findings.remediation: Add explicit provision stating Dova retains all ownership and IP rights in Product Materials and grants Valeant a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use such materials solely for performing Valeant Activities during the Term, with all suggestions/improvements assigned to Dova.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall in good faith reasonably consider all comments and suggestions of Valeant regarding the Promotional Materials.
findings.description: Vague messaging approval standard without dispute resolution for Calendar Year 2019+ materials
findings.reasoning: Unlike Section 4.4.1(a) which grants Dova conclusive determination rights, subsection (b) merely requires Dova to 'reasonably consider' comments for post-2018 materials. There is no mechanism to resolve disagreements if Dova refuses to incorporate messaging Valeant deems necessary for Target Professionals, potentially creating deadlock.
findings.remediation: Clarify that Dova retains final approval authority consistent with Section 4.4.1(a), or establish a JSC escalation procedure with time-bound resolution for messaging disputes specific to Promotional Materials.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall have the right, but not the obligation, to conduct such additional training itself, provided that the Valeant trainers have been trained by Dova, and provided further that Dova shall have the right to attend such training upon reasonable notice by Valeant to Dova.
findings.description: Valeant may conduct unsupervised training without Dova approval of content, materials, or methodology
findings.reasoning: Valeant controls delivery of additional training without requirement to submit training scripts, content, or materials to Dova for approval. While Dova has a right to attend, this is reactive (upon notice) rather than a proactive audit or approval right. Valeant could theoretically deviate from approved messaging during unsupervised training sessions.
findings.remediation: Require Dova's prior written approval of all training content, scripts, and materials used by Valeant in additional training, and grant Dova the right to audit training sessions without prior notice.

findings.clause_text: Valeant will certify in writing to Dova that all Field Force Personnel have completed the training described in this Section 4.4.1(b).
findings.description: Incorrect cross-reference to subsection (b) rather than training provisions
findings.reasoning: Section 4.4.1(b) addresses Promotional Materials content discussions, not training requirements. The training obligations are described in subsections (c), (d), and (e). This clerical error creates ambiguity regarding which specific training completion triggers the certification obligation.
findings.remediation: Correct the cross-reference to 'this Section 4.4.1' or specifically to subsections (c), (d), and (e) to accurately reflect the training completion requirement.

findings.clause_text: Valeant and all Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Valeant Activities shall comply with the applicable provisions of the Code
findings.description: Undefined 'Code' reference creates uncertainty regarding compliance standards
findings.reasoning: The term 'Code' is not defined elsewhere in the provided text. In pharmaceutical contexts, this could refer to the PhRMA Code, IFPMA Code, AdvaMed Code, or other industry ethical codes. This ambiguity creates regulatory risk regarding which specific standards govern interactions with healthcare professionals and reporting obligations.
findings.remediation: Define 'Code' as the 'PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals (as amended from time to time)' or specify the applicable industry code for the relevant jurisdiction.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall have the responsibility for on- going training of its Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing in accordance with customary practice in the pharmaceutical industry.
findings.description: Vague 'customary practice' standard for ongoing training creates uncertainty regarding adequacy and content
findings.reasoning: 'Customary practice' is inherently subjective and varies significantly between pharmaceutical companies, therapeutic areas, and products. This standard cannot be objectively measured to determine breach, potentially leaving Field Force Personnel inadequately trained on Product-specific requirements while Valeant claims compliance.
findings.remediation: Replace with objective standards specifying minimum frequency (e.g., quarterly updates), content requirements (consistent with current Product labeling), or reference to Dova's training standards.

findings.clause_text: N/A - General Section Absence
findings.description: Absence of mutual indemnification for IP infringement and regulatory violations arising from Product Materials
findings.reasoning: Given Dova creates materials that Valeant uses in the field, and both parties have compliance obligations, the absence of indemnification provisions exposes both parties to unlimited liability. Dova is exposed if materials infringe third-party IP; Valeant is exposed for regulatory violations arising from content Dova controls.
findings.remediation: Insert mutual indemnification: Dova indemnifies Valeant for IP infringement and content-based regulatory violations; Valeant indemnifies Dova for violations caused by unauthorized modifications or misuse by Field Force Personnel.

findings.clause_text: N/A - General Section Absence
findings.description: No limitation of liability for breaches of materials preparation, approval, or training obligations
findings.reasoning: The obligations in this section involve high-risk activities (FDA promotional compliance, IP rights, mandatory training). In the absence of liability caps, either party could face unlimited damages for breaches, including consequential damages arising from regulatory enforcement actions or product recalls due to promotional violations.
findings.remediation: Add liability caps (e.g., equal to annual co-promotion fees paid or received under Section 6.3) with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and regulatory violations.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall be solely responsible for ensuring that the Product Materials prepared and approved by it are in compliance with... Applicable Law
findings.description: Missing definition of 'Applicable Law' leaves compliance scope undefined in highly regulated pharmaceutical context
findings.reasoning: The phrase 'Applicable Law' is central to Dova's compliance obligations but is undefined. In a co-promotion arrangement involving FDA-regulated activities, this creates uncertainty regarding whether obligations include federal anti-kickback statutes, state laws, FDA promotional guidelines, Sunshine Act reporting, FCPA, and other regulations. This gap increases regulatory enforcement risk.
findings.remediation: Define 'Applicable Law' comprehensively to include FDA regulations (21 C.F.R.), Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, Anti-Kickback Statute, False Claims Act, FCPA, state pharmacy laws, and applicable industry codes.

findings.clause_text: as consideration for the Valeant Activities performed by Valeant, Dova shall pay Valeant a promotion fee based on annual Net Sales
findings.description: No minimum performance thresholds or metrics required for Valeant to earn promotion fees
findings.reasoning: Valeant is entitled to payment based solely on Net Sales volume regardless of whether their promotional activities actually contributed to those sales or met any performance standards. This creates a unilateral payment obligation for Dova without guaranteed value or accountability for Valeant's performance.
findings.remediation: Add performance milestones, minimum detailing requirements, or market share targets that must be met before fees are payable, or structure as a true commission based on documented Valeant-generated sales only.

findings.clause_text: (a) For any portion of Net Sales up to and equal [***] in a Calendar Year, an amount equal to [***] of such portion of Net Sales; (b) For any portion of Net Sales in excess of [***] and up to and equal [***] in a Calendar Year, an amount equal to [***] of such portion of Net Sales; and (c) For any portion of Net Sales in excess of [***] in a Calendar Year, [***] of such portion of Net Sales
findings.description: No aggregate cap on promotion fees and no right to offset damages or breaches against fees owed
findings.reasoning: The tiered structure continues indefinitely based on sales volume without a maximum payment cap. Additionally, there is no provision allowing Dova to offset amounts owed for indemnification, breach damages, or product liability claims against promotion fees payable to Valeant, creating uncapped payment exposure.
findings.remediation: Negotiate an annual cap on total promotion fees and include explicit offset rights permitting Dova to deduct amounts owed for breaches, indemnification claims, or product liability from current or future promotion fee payments.

findings.clause_text: as consideration for the Valeant Activities performed by Valeant
findings.description: Undefined term 'Valeant Activities' creates uncertainty regarding what services justify the promotion fee
findings.reasoning: The clause references 'Valeant Activities' as the consideration for the fee but does not define what activities are included (e.g., detailing, marketing, medical education). This ambiguity could lead to disputes over whether Valeant is performing sufficient or appropriate activities to justify the fee structure, or whether Dova is paying for activities not actually performed.
findings.remediation: Include a specific definition of 'Valeant Activities' referencing the detailed obligations in the agreement (e.g., detailing, promotional efforts, medical affairs support) and cross-reference to any exhibits detailing specific performance requirements.

findings.clause_text: Commencing with the Calendar Quarter commencing on October 1, 2018
findings.description: Specific historical commencement date may create confusion if agreement is assigned or extended
findings.reasoning: The clause specifies a fixed historical date (October 1, 2018) for commencement of payment obligations. If the agreement is assigned, renewed, or extended, this fixed date may create confusion regarding when payment obligations begin for new parties or terms, potentially triggering unintended payment obligations or disputes over calculation periods.
findings.remediation: Change to 'Commencing with the first Calendar Quarter following the Effective Date' or define 'Commencement Date' in the agreement to allow flexibility for assignment or extension scenarios.

findings.description: Missing payment terms, invoicing procedures, and audit rights
findings.reasoning: Section 6.1.2 is empty despite the heading indicating it should contain critical commercial terms including payment terms, invoicing procedures, and audit rights related to promotion fees. In a co-promotion agreement between pharmaceutical companies, these terms are essential for defining financial obligations between the product owner (Dova) and co-promotion partner (Valeant). The absence of defined payment terms creates uncertainty regarding timing, method, and conditions for payment of promotion fees. Missing invoicing procedures lead to disputes over documentation requirements and payment triggers. The lack of audit rights removes Dova's ability to verify the accuracy of fees paid or expenses claimed by Valeant, creating significant financial exposure, compliance risks under healthcare regulations (Anti-Kickback Statute, Sunshine Act), and potential for undetected overpayment or fraudulent billing.
findings.remediation: Negotiate to include comprehensive provisions specifying: (1) Calculation methodology for promotion fees (e.g., percentage of net sales, fixed fees, or performance-based milestones with specific metrics), (2) Payment schedule including due dates, currency, and method of payment, (3) Late payment interest penalties (e.g., 1.5% per month or maximum legal rate), (4) Detailed invoicing requirements including supporting documentation, certification of accuracy, and dispute resolution timelines, (5) Comprehensive audit rights allowing Dova to examine Valeant's books and records related to promotion activities and fee calculations, with provisions for: (a) audit frequency (e.g., annually or upon reasonable suspicion of error), (b) notice periods (e.g., 30 days), (c) cost allocation (each party bears own costs unless discrepancy exceeds threshold, e.g., 5%, then offending party pays audit costs), (d) confidentiality of audit results, and (e) right to recover overpayments plus interest.

findings.clause_ref: Definition of 'Net Sales' - Verify if defined elsewhere to ensure proper calculation base
findings.clause_text: Definition of 'Net Sales' - Verify if defined elsewhere to ensure proper calculation base
findings.description: The definition of 'Net Sales' is not provided in the current section, creating a coverage gap regarding the calculation base for financial obligations in the co-promotion agreement.
findings.reasoning: In a co-promotion agreement, Net Sales is the fundamental metric for calculating royalties, profit sharing, or other payments owed to Dova Pharmaceuticals. Without a precise definition including permitted deductions (e.g., taxes, returns, discounts, rebates), exclusions (e.g., samples, compassionate use, clinical trials), and calculation methodology, Dova faces significant financial uncertainty and potential disputes over payment amounts. The absence of this definition prevents verification of whether the calculation base is favorable or contains inappropriate deductions that could substantially reduce revenue. Additionally, without clear transfer pricing provisions, Valeant could potentially manipulate intercompany pricing to reduce Net Sales artificially.
findings.remediation: 1. Locate the Net Sales definition in the agreement (likely in Article 6, Section 6.1, or a Definitions section). 2. Ensure the definition includes: (a) specific enumerated permitted deductions with caps if possible; (b) clear exclusions for samples, compassionate use, clinical trial supplies, and other non-revenue generating distributions; (c) methodology for handling bundled products or combination therapies; (d) currency conversion rules and timing; (e) transfer pricing protections requiring arms-length pricing; (f) most favored customer pricing protections if applicable. 3. If the definition allows excessive deductions or lacks specificity, negotiate to limit deductions to those customary in the pharmaceutical industry (typically limited to returns, rebates, and customary discounts) and require detailed quarterly reporting to verify calculations. 4. Ensure Dova has audit rights over Valeant's Net Sales calculations.

findings.description: Missing definition of 'Valeant Activities' creates unquantifiable scope and liability exposure
findings.reasoning: In a co-promotion agreement, the definition of activities determines the scope of Valeant's promotional obligations, expense allocation, regulatory compliance duties, and territorial limitations. Without this definition, Dova cannot assess: (1) whether Valeant's obligations are sufficiently defined to enforce performance; (2) which party bears costs for specific activities; (3) liability exposure for off-label promotion or regulatory violations; and (4) whether activities are limited to specific territories or indications. This gap renders the entire co-promotion structure unenforceable and exposes Dova to unlimited liability for Valeant's actions.
findings.remediation: Immediate negotiation position: (1) Suspend execution until definition is located and reviewed; (2) Definition must explicitly include: specific promotional activities (detailing, sampling, educational programs), excluded activities (formulary negotiations, pricing decisions), geographic scope, target audience (physicians, institutions), performance metrics (call frequency, reach), and regulatory compliance obligations; (3) Ensure definition includes 'no authority to bind' language; (4) Add explicit statement that Valeant acts as independent contractor, not agent of Dova, to limit vicarious liability.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall pay Valeant a promotion fee based on annual Net Sales during the Term
findings.description: The term 'Net Sales' is used as the exclusive calculation base for promotion fees but is not defined in this section or cross-referenced to a defined term.
findings.reasoning: Without a precise definition of Net Sales (including permitted deductions for returns, rebates, chargebacks, taxes, shipping, and timing of recognition), Dova faces unquantifiable exposure to disputed calculations and potential overpayment. This is the entire financial basis of the agreement, and ambiguity here creates significant litigation risk over the interpretation of gross vs. net revenue.
findings.remediation: Add an explicit definition of 'Net Sales' in this section or cross-reference to Article 1 definitions that specifies: (a) gross invoice price less (b) specific deductions (returns, rebates, chargebacks, Medicaid/Medicare rebates, discounts, taxes, freight), (c) timing of recognition (accrual vs. cash), and (d) allocation rules for bundled sales.

findings.clause_text: as consideration for the Valeant Activities performed by Valeant
findings.description: The scope of 'Valeant Activities' is undefined, creating uncertainty regarding what specific promotional services justify the payment of promotion fees.
findings.reasoning: The promotion fee is explicitly consideration for 'Valeant Activities,' yet without a defined scope of work, performance standards, deliverables, or minimum service levels, Valeant could theoretically collect fees while performing minimal, ineffective, or no promotional activities. This creates a severe misalignment of incentives where Valeant is paid based on Dova's sales success (or market factors) regardless of Valeant's actual contribution, effectively converting a co-promotion into a royalty-bearing license without performance obligations.
findings.remediation: Define 'Valeant Activities' with specificity in Article 1 (e.g., detailing sales force deployment levels, call volume targets, medical education activities, formulary access efforts). Add performance metrics or minimum service levels that must be met as a condition precedent to earning promotion fees, including a right to reduce fees proportionally if performance standards are not met.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall pay Valeant a promotion fee based on annual Net Sales during the Term, calculated as follows: [tiered structure]
findings.description: The fee structure is purely sales-based without any performance thresholds, minimum activity requirements, clawback provisions, or offsets for Valeant's breach or failure to perform.
findings.reasoning: Valeant earns fees based solely on Net Sales achieved (presumably by Dova or jointly), regardless of whether Valeant actually performed any promotional activities or performed them effectively. This creates a 'free rider' risk where Valeant benefits from Dova's independent sales efforts or general market success without commensurate effort. Standard co-promotion agreements include minimum performance thresholds (e.g., call volumes, reach/frequency targets) that, if not met, result in fee reduction or termination rights. The absence of such protections forces Dova to pay fees even if Valeant is in breach or non-performance.
findings.remediation: Add performance-based conditions precedent: (a) specify minimum sales force deployment levels or FTE commitments, (b) establish quarterly call volume or reach/frequency targets, (c) provide for pro-rata reduction of promotion fees if Valeant fails to meet defined performance standards, and (d) include a right to set off promotion fees against damages for Valeant's breach or indemnification obligations.

findings.clause_text: For any portion of Net Sales in excess of [***] in a Calendar Year, [***] of such portion of Net Sales
findings.description: The tiered royalty structure continues indefinitely without an aggregate annual cap on total promotion fees payable.
findings.reasoning: While the percentage rates may decrease in higher tiers (redacted), there is no stated maximum dollar cap on annual promotion fees. If the product achieves blockbuster status or unexpected market success, Dova could face unlimited promotion fee obligations that erode profitability and fail to account for Dova's own development and commercialization costs. Standard agreements often include an annual aggregate cap or a reduced percentage tier (e.g., single digits) for sales above a very high threshold to preserve economic viability and align incentives at extreme success levels.
findings.remediation: Negotiate an aggregate annual cap on promotion fees (e.g., 'In no event shall the total promotion fees payable in any Calendar Year exceed $[XXX]') or add a final tier with a significantly reduced percentage (e.g., 5% or less) for sales exceeding a high threshold (e.g., $500M) to limit exposure at extreme sales levels.

findings.clause_text: Commencing with the Calendar Quarter commencing on October 1, 2018
findings.description: The clause specifies a fixed historical date (October 1, 2018) for commencement of fee obligations without reference to the actual Effective Date or term of the agreement.
findings.reasoning: The specific reference to 'October 1, 2018' creates potential confusion regarding retroactive application, true-up calculations, or alignment with the actual agreement term. If this agreement is an amendment, restatement, assignment, or extension, the fixed historical date may trigger unintended payment obligations for historical periods or create ambiguity about whether the date should be updated. This creates exposure for disputes over whether fees are owed for periods prior to actual execution or effective date of current terms.
findings.remediation: Replace the specific historical date with 'the first Calendar Quarter following the Effective Date' or define a 'Promotion Fee Commencement Date' in the definitions section that can be updated if the agreement is amended or assigned. If the historical date is intentional for true-up purposes, explicitly state that this is a retroactive adjustment for the period from October 1, 2018 to the Effective Date, and specify the go-forward calculation method separately.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall pay Valeant a promotion fee based on annual Net Sales
findings.description: The section establishes payment obligations based on Net Sales but does not provide Dova with audit rights to verify the accuracy of Net Sales calculations or payments.
findings.reasoning: Without explicit audit rights, Dova lacks any contractual mechanism to verify that Net Sales are being calculated correctly (including proper application of deductions, credits, and returns) or that promotion fee payments are accurate. This creates information asymmetry where Valeant (if controlling sales data) or Dova (if self-reporting) could miscalculate without detection. Standard financial provisions in co-promotion agreements include comprehensive audit rights with specific procedures, scope limitations, and cost allocation.
findings.remediation: Add a provision granting Dova (and/or Valeant, if reciprocal) the right to audit the other party's books and records related to Net Sales calculations and promotion fee payments, including: (a) annual audit rights with [30-60] days advance notice, (b) scope covering all sales records, deduction documentation, and calculation worksheets, (c) confidentiality protections for audited information, (d) cost allocation (auditing party pays unless error exceeds [5-10]%, then audited party pays), and (e) right to recover overpayments plus interest if discrepancies are found.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall pay Valeant a promotion fee
findings.description: The clause creates an absolute payment obligation without reserving Dova's right to set off amounts owed against damages, breaches, or indemnification claims against Valeant.
findings.reasoning: The unconditional language 'shall pay' does not account for situations where Valeant may owe Dova money (e.g., for breach of contract, indemnification claims for third-party liability, or damage to Dova's business). Without explicit set-off rights, Dova may be required to pay full promotion fees to Valeant while separately pursuing Valeant for damages, creating cash flow disadvantages, increased administrative burden, and potential insolvency risk if Valeant becomes unable to pay judgments while continuing to receive fees. Standard contracts include mutual set-off rights or at least allow the paying party to deduct known, undisputed, or adjudicated amounts owed to it.
findings.remediation: Add explicit set-off language: 'Dova shall have the right to set off any promotion fees owed to Valeant against: (a) damages for Valeant's material breach of this Agreement, (b) indemnification payments owed by Valeant to Dova under Article [X], (c) undisputed amounts owed by Valeant to Dova under this Agreement, and (d) amounts determined by final non-appealable judgment or arbitration award. Dova shall provide written notice of any set-off exercised hereunder.'

findings.description: Critical commercial terms including sales thresholds and percentage rates are redacted, preventing complete assessment of economic burden and risk allocation.
findings.reasoning: While redaction of specific dollar amounts and percentages is standard practice in SEC public filings, the absence of these values prevents assessment of whether the tiered structure creates excessive economic burden (e.g., high percentages in upper tiers without caps) or includes unreasonable cliff effects. This is a coverage limitation rather than a contractual defect, but it masks potential high-severity risks in the underlying commercial terms.
findings.remediation: Obtain the unredacted agreement to review actual percentage rates and threshold amounts. Assess whether: (a) initial tiers are below industry standard co-promotion rates (typically 20-45%), (b) upper tiers decrease sufficiently to preserve Dova's margin, and (c) thresholds are achievable or create perverse incentives. Negotiate caps or reduced rates if upper tier percentages exceed single digits.

findings.clause_text: If the aggregate actual number of Details for the Product made by the Sales Representatives for a Calendar Quarter is less than the Quarterly Minimum Details for such Calendar Quarter, then in calculating the promotion fee due under Section 6.1.1, the Applicable Percentage for such Calendar Quarter shall be reduced to a new percentage equal to [***].
findings.description: Unilateral fee reduction mechanism with redacted penalty percentage creates unquantifiable financial exposure for Dova
findings.reasoning: As outside counsel for Dova (product owner), this clause exposes Dova to potentially severe fee reductions when Valeant underperforms, yet the actual penalty percentages are redacted [***]. The reduction is automatic upon underperformance, with no cure period, no notice requirement, and no minimum floor specified. Dova bears the revenue risk of Valeant's sales force underperformance without visibility into the severity of the penalty. The lack of defined [***] values prevents proper risk assessment.
findings.remediation: Negotiate to: (1) disclose and cap the reduction percentage at no more than [suggested: 25-30%] of original rate; (2) add cure period of [suggested: 30-45 days] to allow remediation before reduction applies; (3) establish floor on minimum percentage payable; (4) require written notice and opportunity to cure; (5) consider making reduction prospective only rather than retroactive to entire quarter

findings.clause_text: If the Quarterly Average Sales Force Size is less than [***] Sales Representatives for an applicable Calendar Quarter, then in calculating the promotion fee due under Section 6.1.1, the Applicable Percentage for such Calendar Quarter shall be reduced to a new percentage equal to [***].
findings.description: Dual-trigger fee reduction based on headcount metric with undisclosed thresholds and penalties
findings.reasoning: This creates a second independent basis for fee reduction based on Valeant's staffing decisions—factors largely within Valeant's control. The [***] thresholds for both minimum headcount and resulting penalty percentage are concealed, preventing Dova from modeling financial exposure. Valeant could strategically reduce headcount to trigger this provision while still satisfying minimum Detail obligations through other means. The double-reduction risk in 6.1.2(c) compounds exposure.
findings.remediation: Negotiate to: (1) set the headcount threshold at [suggested: 80-85%] of contracted FTEs rather than absolute number; (2) cap reduction percentage and require proportionality between headcount shortfall and percentage reduction; (3) exclude reductions where headcount reduction is due to market conditions beyond Valeant's control; (4) require advance notice of planned headcount changes; (5) eliminate subsection (c) 'lower of' stacking and instead apply most favorable-to-Dova calculation or limit to single trigger

findings.clause_text: In the event that subsections (a) above and (b) above are both applicable in an applicable Calendar Quarter, then the Applicable Percentage shall be reduced to a new percentage equal to the lower of the percentages calculated under subsections (a) and (b).
findings.description: Stacking of penalties via 'lower of' selection mechanism maximizes Dova's fee reduction exposure
findings.reasoning: The 'lower of' formulation is extraordinarily unfavorable to Dova. When both triggers occur (underperformance on Details AND headcount shortfall), Dova receives the worst possible rate rather than a blended or capped reduction. This creates compounding asymmetry: Valeant's multiple failures produce multiplicative penalties to Dova's revenue. No commercial justification exists for selecting the more severe penalty when Valeant breaches multiple obligations simultaneously. This structure incentivizes Valeant to underperform on both metrics.
findings.remediation: CRITICAL: Replace 'lower of' with 'higher of' or, preferably, eliminate stacking entirely by applying only subsection (a) (performance-based) or capping total reduction at [suggested: 35%] regardless of trigger combination. Alternative: apply reductions sequentially with floor. Must also add anti-abuse language preventing deliberate triggering of dual penalties through coordinated underperformance

findings.clause_text: [Empty/Redacted - Section 4.1.2 contains no visible text; content appears to be fully redacted with placeholder or missing entirely]
