findings.clause_text: Valeant shall instruct the Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing to conduct the Valeant Activities for the Product, and will monitor and audit (in accordance with Valeant's standard practice) the Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing so that such personnel conduct the Valeant Activities for the Product in adherence in all respects with Applicable Laws.
findings.description: Monitoring and audit obligations are entirely subjective, tied to Valeant's internal standards without objective benchmarks, Dova oversight rights, or regulatory specificity
findings.reasoning: The phrase 'in accordance with Valeant's standard practice' renders compliance self-judging and unverifiable. Valeant could theoretically meet this obligation with minimal or ineffective monitoring. No requirement exists for: (1) minimum audit frequency; (2) Dova participation in or review of audit results; (3) remediation timelines for identified violations; (4) escalation to Dova of serious compliance failures. This creates severe exposure for Dova if Valeant's 'standard practice' proves inadequate, particularly given pharmaceutical co-promotion's strict liability risks under the FDCA and potential False Claims Act exposure from off-label promotion.
findings.remediation: Replace subjective standard with: (1) minimum quarterly audits of at least 10% of Field Force Personnel with documented reports; (2) Dova right to receive all audit reports within 10 business days and conduct parallel audits; (3) mandatory 48-hour escalation of any suspected off-label promotion or adverse event reporting failures; (4) independent third-party audit right for Dova if two or more material violations are found in any 12-month period; (5) immediate suspension right for Dova upon reasonable belief of serious regulatory violation; (6) specific reference to FDA OPDP guidance and PhRMA Code as minimum standards

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall instruct the Field Force Personnel that are engaged in Detailing regarding provisions of this Agreement applicable to Details of the Product, including Section 4.2 and this Section 4.5.1.
findings.description: Training obligation is limited to 'provisions of this Agreement' without requiring training on Product Labeling, adverse event reporting, or regulatory compliance standards
findings.reasoning: The training mandate is narrowly cabined to contractual provisions rather than substantive compliance requirements. Field Force Personnel could be technically 'instructed' on Section 4.2 and 4.5.1 without understanding: (1) actual Product indications and contraindications; (2) adverse event identification and reporting obligations (critical for pharmacovigilance); (3) anti-kickback and fraud/abuse laws; (4) state licensing requirements. This creates gap between contractual compliance and operational regulatory compliance.
findings.remediation: Expand to require: (1) initial and annual training on complete Product Labeling, including all boxed warnings and contraindications; (2) certified training on adverse event reporting with documentation maintained for FDA inspection; (3) training on applicable federal and state healthcare compliance laws; (4) Dova's right to approve training curriculum and materials; (5) training completion certificates provided to Dova; (6) retraining within 30 days of any material compliance failure

findings.clause_text: Valeant acknowledges and agrees that Dova will not maintain or procure any worker's compensation, healthcare, or other insurance for or on behalf of the Field Force Personnel, all of which shall be Valeant's sole responsibility.
findings.description: Insurance disclaimer lacks requirement for Valeant to maintain specific coverage types or minimum limits, and omits naming Dova as additional insured
findings.reasoning: While Valeant assumes responsibility, there is no enforcement mechanism ensuring actual coverage exists. No requirement for: (1) general liability insurance covering bodily injury/property damage from detailing activities; (2) professional liability/errors & omissions for promotional activities; (3) cyber liability for PHI exposure; (4) minimum coverage limits; (5) Dova as additional insured or certificate of insurance provision. If Valeant becomes insolvent or underinsured, Dova faces direct liability for Field Force Personnel actions without recourse.
findings.remediation: Add: (1) minimum $5M per occurrence/$10M aggregate general liability; (2) $5M professional liability for regulatory/compliance failures; (3) $5M cyber liability for PHI breaches; (4) Dova named as additional insured on all policies; (5) annual certificates of insurance delivered to Dova; (6) 30-day notice of cancellation; (7) right to terminate Agreement immediately upon lapse of required coverage; (8) Valeant obligation to maintain coverage for claims arising during term for minimum 5 years post-termination

findings.clause_text: Valeant acknowledges and agrees that all Field Force Personnel are employees of Valeant and are not, and are not intended to be treated as, employees of Dova or any of its Affiliates, and that such individuals are not, and are not intended to be, eligible to participate in any benefits programs or in any 'employee benefit plans' (as such term is defined in section 3(3) of ERISA) that are sponsored by Dova or any of its Affiliates or that are offered from time to time by Dova or its Affiliates to their own employees. All matters of compensation, benefits and other terms of employment for any such Field Force Personnel shall be solely a matter between Valeant and such individual. Dova shall not be responsible to Valeant, or to the Field Force Personnel, for any compensation, expense reimbursements or benefits (including vacation and holiday remuneration, healthcare coverage or insurance, life insurance, severance or termination of employment benefits, pension or profit-sharing benefits and disability benefits), payroll-related taxes or withholdings, or any governmental charges or benefits (including unemployment and disability insurance contributions or benefits and workmen's compensation contributions or benefits) that may be imposed upon or be related to the performance by Valeant or such individuals of this Agreement, all of which shall be the sole responsibility of Valeant, even if it is subsequently determined by any Governmental Authority that any such individual may be an employee or a common law employee of Dova or any of its Affiliates or is otherwise entitled to such payments and benefits.
findings.description: Joint employer liability disclaimer is contractually asserted but legally unenforceable as to third parties, with no indemnification for defense costs, regulatory penalties, or operational disruption from reclassification
findings.reasoning: The 'even if' clause attempts contractual allocation of liability that courts and agencies (DOL, IRS, state agencies) may disregard in determining joint employer status. The clause provides zero protection for Dova when: (1) Field Force Personnel file wage/hour claims naming Dova; (2) IRS challenges employment tax treatment; (3) union organizing occurs with Dova named as joint employer; (4) state agencies assess unemployment taxes. Most critically, there is no indemnification obligation requiring Valeant to defend Dova, pay settlements/judgments, or cover regulatory penalties. The 'sole responsibility' language is merely a promise to pay benefits, not a comprehensive indemnity. Dova bears full defense costs and business disruption without recourse.
findings.remediation: Add comprehensive indemnification: (1) Valeant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Dova from all claims, losses, damages, penalties, and costs (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from any determination of joint employer status, misclassification, or any employment-related claim by Field Force Personnel; (2) immediate reimbursement of all defense costs without cap; (3) Valeant obligation to post bond or security if financially distressed; (4) Dova right to control defense of any claim naming both parties; (5) mutual cooperation in opposing joint employer findings; (6) termination right if Valeant fails to timely indemnify; (7) survival of indemnity obligations for minimum 6 years post-termination

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall be solely responsible for the acts or omissions of the Field Force Personnel that are not in compliance with Applicable Law and the terms of this Agreement while performing any of the activities under this Agreement. Valeant shall be solely responsible and liable for all probationary and termination actions taken by it, as well as for the formulation, content and dissemination (including content) of all employment policies and rules (including written probationary and termination policies) applicable to its employees.
findings.description: Valeant's responsibility is ambiguously limited to 'not in compliance' acts, potentially excluding liability for compliant acts that cause harm, and lacks indemnification for third-party claims
findings.reasoning: The limitation to acts 'not in compliance with Applicable Law and the terms of this Agreement' creates a dangerous carve-out. If Field Force Personnel follow Valeant's instructions (which Valeant believes comply) but cause patient harm, product liability, or data breach, Valeant could argue the acts were 'in compliance' and thus excluded from this clause. This creates: (1) evidentiary burden on Dova to prove non-compliance; (2) coverage gap for negligent but non-violative acts; (3) no clear indemnification for third-party claims (patients, healthcare providers, regulators). The second sentence addresses only employment policies, not operational liability. No cross-indemnification exists for product liability, personal injury, or regulatory enforcement.
findings.remediation: Revise to: (1) 'Valeant shall be solely responsible for all acts or omissions of Field Force Personnel, whether or not in compliance with Applicable Law or this Agreement, and shall indemnify Dova for all claims, damages, and costs arising therefrom'; (2) explicitly include product liability, personal injury, privacy breaches, and regulatory enforcement actions; (3) remove compliance-based limitation entirely; (4) add mutual indemnification for Dova's own negligence or Product defects; (5) specify Valeant's insurance must cover these obligations; (6) no monetary cap on Valeant's indemnity obligations

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall be solely responsible for any and all costs and expenses incurred by Valeant or any of its Affiliates in connection with the conduct of the Valeant Activities for the Product hereunder, including all costs and expenses in connection with Sales Representatives, including salaries, travel expenses and other expenses, credentialing, licensing, providing benefits, deducting federal, state and local payroll taxes, and paying workers' compensation premiums, unemployment insurance contributions and any other payments required by Applicable Laws to be made on behalf of employees.
findings.description: Absence of indemnification and insurance requirements for employment-related liabilities creates joint employer exposure for Dova despite cost allocation to Valeant.
findings.reasoning: While the clause allocates financial responsibility to Valeant, it fails to protect Dova from joint employer liability or statutory employer claims that may arise from Valeant's sales representatives promoting Dova's product. In co-promotion arrangements, Dova typically directs the promotional activities and messaging of Valeant's reps, creating significant risk that courts or regulators will deem Dova a joint employer. Without explicit indemnification and insurance requirements, Dova remains exposed to wage/hour class actions, discrimination claims, and statutory penalties (including payroll tax deficiencies) if Valeant—who has historically faced financial distress—fails to properly classify employees, maintain coverage, or pay required contributions. The clause addresses 'who pays' but not 'who bears liability' to third parties.
findings.remediation: Add explicit language requiring Valeant to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Dova from any claims arising out of or relating to the employment or engagement of Sales Representatives, including misclassification claims, wage/hour violations, employment discrimination, and statutory employer claims. Require Valeant to maintain Employment Practices Liability Insurance (EPLI) with limits of not less than $5 million per occurrence and Workers' Compensation insurance as required by statute, naming Dova as an additional insured on both policies, with certificates of insurance provided to Dova annually and upon request.

findings.clause_text: including all costs and expenses in connection with... credentialing, licensing
findings.description: Regulatory liability exposure due to lack of audit rights, compliance verification, and indemnification for Valeant's credentialing and licensing failures.
findings.reasoning: If Valeant fails to properly credential or license its sales representatives (e.g., maintaining required pharmaceutical representative licenses, FLMA certifications, or compliance with state-specific requirements), and such unqualified reps engage in off-label promotion, misleading marketing, or violations of the Anti-Kickback Statute while detailing Dova's product, Dova faces severe regulatory exposure including FDA enforcement actions, OIG scrutiny, and potential False Claims Act qui tam suits. The current clause lacks: (1) audit rights for Dova to verify compliance; (2) immediate reporting obligations for lapses; (3) standards for credentialing; and (4) explicit indemnification for regulatory penalties arising from credentialing failures. Given that Dova is the product owner/NDA holder, regulatory violations by Valeant's unlicensed reps will primarily impact Dova's regulatory standing and expose Dova to corporate integrity agreements or debarment.
findings.remediation: Add specific covenants requiring Valeant to: (a) maintain all Sales Representatives in good standing with all necessary federal, state, and local licenses and credentials; (b) ensure all reps complete Dova-approved compliance training; (c) grant Dova quarterly audit rights to verify credentialing status and inspect licenses; (d) provide immediate written notice (within 24 hours) of any licensing lapses, suspensions, or regulatory inquiries; and (e) explicitly indemnify Dova for any regulatory fines, penalties, enforcement actions, or exclusion from federal healthcare programs arising from Valeant's failure to properly credential, license, or supervise its Sales Representatives.

findings.clause_text: Other than as expressly set out herein, Valeant shall be solely responsible...
findings.description: Ambiguous cross-referencing creates risk of unintended cost-sharing obligations and scope creep.
findings.reasoning: The carve-out 'Other than as expressly set out herein' suggests Dova may have explicit cost obligations elsewhere in the agreement regarding Valeant Activities or Sales Representative costs. Without specific cross-references to the sections containing such exceptions, this language creates interpretive ambiguity and potential for disputes regarding which party bears specific costs (e.g., joint training costs, pharmacovigilance reporting costs, promotional material development, or regulatory filing fees). This ambiguity exposes Dova to claims that it agreed to share costs it assumed were solely Valeant's responsibility, particularly in wind-down scenarios or termination disputes.
findings.remediation: Either (Option A) delete the 'Other than as expressly set out herein' preamble if Dova has no cost obligations for the enumerated categories (Sales Reps, taxes, workers comp, etc.), replacing with 'Valeant shall be solely responsible for all costs and expenses...'; or (Option B) if exceptions exist, add specific parenthetical cross-references such as '(other than as set forth in Sections [X.Y] and [Z.A])' to provide clarity and prevent scope disputes.

findings.clause_text: paying workers' compensation premiums, unemployment insurance contributions and any other payments required by Applicable Laws
findings.description: No verification mechanism or default remedies for statutory payment compliance, exposing Dova to successor liability and statutory lien claims.
findings.reasoning: If Valeant fails to remit workers' compensation premiums, unemployment insurance contributions, or payroll taxes—particularly given Valeant's historical financial volatility—statutory schemes in many jurisdictions permit claimants to pursue the 'principal' (Dova) under joint and several liability theories or statutory employer doctrines. Injured sales representatives or tax authorities may place liens on Dova's assets or seek direct recovery from Dova if Valeant becomes insolvent or defaults. The clause lacks: (1) audit rights to verify payments; (2) requirements for certificates of insurance; (3) representations regarding compliance history; and (4) termination rights for Dova if Valeant defaults on these statutory obligations.
findings.remediation: Add requirements that Valeant: (a) provide annual certificates of insurance for workers' compensation and unemployment insurance naming Dova as certificate holder; (b) represent and warrant that all such premiums and contributions are current with no pending claims or defaults; (c) grant Dova audit rights upon 30 days' notice to inspect payroll records and tax filings; and (d) acknowledge that failure to maintain these payments constitutes a material breach permitting immediate termination by Dova.

findings.description: Critical definition of 'Valeant Activities' is entirely missing despite governing cost allocation, scope of work, and reimbursement obligations between Dova and Valeant
findings.reasoning: In a co-promotion agreement, the definition of activities determines which party bears costs and what promotional work is authorized. Without a precise, exhaustive definition of 'Valeant Activities', Valeant can unilaterally characterize any promotional activity, general overhead, or even activities for other products as falling within this definition and charge costs to Dova. This creates unlimited cost exposure, uncontrolled scope creep, and inevitable disputes over what constitutes reimbursable activity versus Valeant's standard business operations. Given Valeant's historical reputation for aggressive cost allocation practices, this omission exposes Dova to significant financial and operational risk.
findings.remediation: Negotiate a comprehensive, exhaustive definition that: (1) specifically lists all permitted Valeant Activities by category with detailed descriptions (e.g., physician detailing, speaker programs, medical education, formulary access support); (2) explicitly excludes certain activities (e.g., activities for other Valeant products, general administrative overhead, corporate functions, market research not specific to the product); (3) requires written pre-approval from Dova for any activities outside the defined scope or exceeding budgeted amounts; (4) caps the total cost allocation or requires activity-based budgeting with quarterly reconciliation; (5) includes a 'most favored customer' clause ensuring Dova doesn't pay higher rates than other co-promotion partners for similar activities; and (6) specifies that only activities actually performed and documented according to specified standards are reimbursable.

findings.description: Critical definitional section is entirely absent, creating severe employment tax, joint employer liability, and regulatory compliance exposure in the co-promotion arrangement
findings.reasoning: The lack of a defined term for 'Sales Representatives'—particularly regarding the inclusion/exclusion of agency, temporary, or contract workers—creates catastrophic ambiguity in a pharmaceutical co-promotion context. Without this definition: (1) Dova faces unallocated employment tax withholding obligations and IRS/ DOL misclassification penalties; (2) Valeant's temporary workers may be deemed Dova's statutory employees under joint employer theories (FLSA, NLRA, state wage/hour laws), triggering unexpected benefit plan eligibility and workers' compensation liabilities; (3) FDA regulatory responsibility for promotional activities and adverse event reporting by non-employee representatives remains unallocated; and (4) indemnification triggers for representative misconduct cannot be enforced with certainty. The parenthetical reference to 'different tax implications' in the section title suggests the parties recognized this classification risk but failed to memorialize the resolution, leaving Dova exposed to Valeant's staffing decisions.
findings.remediation: Insert a comprehensive definition explicitly excluding temporary, agency, or contract workers from the definition of 'Sales Representatives' unless specifically agreed. If inclusion is necessary: (a) require Valeant to indemnify Dova for all employment taxes, unemployment insurance, workers' compensation claims, and benefit plan liabilities arising from such classification; (b) allocate exclusive employer status to Valeant for all statutory purposes; (c) require Valeant to maintain EPLI and statutory employment coverage for temporary staff; and (d) specify that Dova's training, supervision, and compliance obligations apply only to Valeant's direct W-2 employees. Add representations that Valeant is solely responsible for tax withholding and reporting for any non-employee representatives.

findings.clause_ref: Section cross-references regarding other cost obligations referenced in 'Other than as expressly set out herein'
findings.clause_text: [No clause text provided - Section content is empty or undefined]
findings.description: Missing cross-references to cost obligations combined with exclusionary 'Other than as expressly set out herein' language creates unlimited exposure for unfunded promotional, regulatory, and pharmacovigilance costs
findings.reasoning: In co-promotion agreements, 'Other than as expressly set out herein' operates as a strict limitation on obligation-to-pay, requiring exhaustive enumeration of all shared costs elsewhere in the agreement. The absence of specific cross-references to Development Costs, Commercialization Costs, Regulatory Costs, Medical Affairs Costs, and Pharmacovigilance Costs renders the cost-sharing framework unenforceable or heavily biased against the Product Owner. As outside counsel for Dova, this exposes Dova to sole funding of ambiguous costs (e.g., safety reporting, promotional review, sampling) that Valeant may dispute as not being 'expressly set out' in the referenced sections, potentially shifting 100% of undefined costs to Dova despite the co-promotion structure.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive Schedule X (Cost Allocation) explicitly listing all cost categories with allocation keys (e.g., 'Regulatory filing fees: 50/50', 'Pharmacovigilance costs: 50/50', 'Product supply manufacturing: 100% Dova', 'Field force detailing costs: respective party costs'). Replace 'Other than as expressly set out herein' with 'Subject to and in accordance with the cost allocation principles set forth in Schedule X and Sections [Y-Z]'. Add specific cross-references to: Development Cost definitions (Section X.X), Commercialization Cost definitions (Section X.X), Regulatory Cost definitions (Section X.X), and Pharmacovigilance Cost definitions (Section X.X). Include a catch-all 'Shared Costs' definition for expenses not specifically allocated to one party.

findings.clause_text: Valeant shall be solely responsible for any and all costs and expenses incurred by Valeant or any of its Affiliates in connection with the conduct of the Valeant Activities for the Product hereunder, including all costs and expenses in connection with Sales Representatives, including salaries, travel expenses and other expenses, credentialing, licensing, providing benefits, deducting federal, state and local payroll taxes, and paying workers' compensation premiums, unemployment insurance contributions and any other payments required by Applicable Laws to be made on behalf of employees.
findings.description: Absence of indemnification and insurance requirements for employment-related liabilities creates joint employer exposure for Dova despite cost allocation to Valeant.
findings.reasoning: While Valeant assumes financial responsibility for employment costs, the clause lacks (1) indemnification for claims arising from employment practices (wrongful termination, discrimination, wage/hour violations, harassment) brought against Dova; (2) requirements for Employment Practices Liability Insurance (EPLI); and (3) contractual joint employer avoidance provisions. Courts routinely find pharmaceutical co-promotion partners jointly liable for labor law violations involving detailing staff, exposing Dova to unlimited liability without recourse.
findings.remediation: Add comprehensive indemnification requiring Valeant to defend and hold Dova harmless from all employment-related claims. Require Valeant to maintain EPLI with adequate limits (minimum $5M), workers' compensation, and statutory disability insurance. Include explicit disclaimers of joint employer status and agency.

findings.clause_text: deducting federal, state and local payroll taxes, and paying workers' compensation premiums, unemployment insurance contributions and any other payments required by Applicable Laws to be made on behalf of employees
findings.description: No verification mechanism or default remedies for statutory payment compliance, exposing Dova to successor liability and statutory lien claims.
findings.reasoning: Valeant's obligation to remit payroll taxes and insurance premiums lacks audit rights, periodic certification requirements, or remedies upon default. If Valeant becomes insolvent, fails to remit taxes, or misclassifies employees as independent contractors, Dova faces successor liability under IRC Section 3505, state tax liens, and uninsured workers' compensation claims as the beneficiary of the sales activities.
findings.remediation: Require quarterly certifications of tax compliance and proof of workers' compensation coverage. Grant Dova audit rights over payroll records. Require Valeant to indemnify Dova for any tax deficiencies, penalties, or interest. Consider requiring an escrow or letter of credit for statutory obligations.

findings.clause_text: Other than as expressly set out herein, Valeant shall be solely responsible for any and all costs and expenses
findings.description: Unlimited cost obligation without monetary cap, liability limitation, or definition of excluded costs creates unquantified financial exposure.
findings.reasoning: The phrase 'any and all costs and expenses' imposes unlimited financial liability on Valeant but provides no aggregate cap, budget mechanism, or carve-out for extraordinary costs (pandemic-related safety, regulatory mandated training, litigation hold expenses). The 'Other than as expressly set out herein' language creates ambiguity regarding Dova's potential obligations without defining what is 'expressly set out', leading to disputes over unfunded regulatory, medical affairs, or pharmacovigilance costs.
findings.remediation: Insert an annual budget cap for Valeant Activities. Replace 'any and all' with 'reasonable and documented costs directly attributable to Valeant Activities as specified in Exhibit [X]'. Replace blanket exclusion with specific cross-references to sections where Dova obligations are defined. Exclude consequential damages and indirect costs.

findings.clause_text: credentialing, licensing... and any other payments required by Applicable Laws
findings.description: Regulatory liability exposure due to lack of audit rights, compliance verification, and indemnification for Valeant's credentialing and licensing failures.
findings.reasoning: Valeant's responsibility for sales representative credentialing and licensing carries inherent regulatory risk (FDA debarment, OIG exclusion, state licensing board actions). The clause lacks standards for credential maintenance (e.g., DEA licenses, state pharmacy licenses), audit rights to verify active credentials, cure periods for lapses, or indemnification if credentialing failures result in regulatory action against the Product or Dova.
findings.remediation: Add specific compliance standards requiring all reps to hold valid, active licenses with no exclusions. Grant Dova right to audit credential status quarterly. Require immediate cure for any lapsed credentials. Add indemnification for regulatory fines, product promotion bans, or debarment proceedings arising from Valeant's credentialing failures.

findings.clause_text: in connection with the conduct of the Valeant Activities for the Product hereunder
findings.description: Critical definition of 'Valeant Activities' is entirely missing despite governing cost allocation, scope of work, and reimbursement obligations between Dova and Valeant.
findings.reasoning: The clause allocates all costs to 'Valeant Activities' but this defined term is absent from the provided sections. This definitional gap creates fatal ambiguity regarding scope: disputed activities (pharmacovigilance reporting, medical information calls, regulatory inspections, KOL engagements) may be claimed by Valeant as reimbursable costs or disputed as Dova responsibilities, leading to litigation over millions in unfunded obligations.
findings.remediation: Add comprehensive definition: 'Valeant Activities' means specific detailing and promotional activities listed in Schedule [X], explicitly excluding pharmacovigilance, medical affairs, regulatory compliance, and clinical trials. Include illustrative examples and negative covenants.

findings.clause_text: Other than as expressly set out herein
findings.description: Ambiguous cross-referencing creates risk of unintended cost-sharing obligations and scope creep.
findings.reasoning: The exclusionary phrase 'Other than as expressly set out herein' creates interpretive uncertainty. Without specific section references, parties may dispute whether costs mentioned in general terms elsewhere (e.g., 'each Party bears its own costs' in a termination clause) constitute 'express' allocation overriding Section 4.6. This ambiguity invites litigation over shared costs like pharmacovigilance systems, regulatory filings, or product liability defense.
findings.remediation: Delete ambiguous phrase and replace with specific enumeration: 'Except for costs allocated to Dova pursuant to Sections [X.Y, Z.W], Valeant shall be responsible...' or attach a schedule listing specific excluded costs.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information relating to the sale, commercialization, marketing and promotion of the Product, as may be mutually agreed by the Parties from time to time
findings.description: Unfettered obligation to provide sales and marketing data without specificity, carve-outs for competitively sensitive information, or reciprocity requirements
findings.reasoning: The phrase 'certain information' is undefined and could encompass pricing strategies, profit margins, customer lists, and trade secrets. In a co-promotion arrangement with Valeant (now Bausch Health), a major pharmaceutical entity with potentially competing products or acquisition targets, this creates significant competitive intelligence risk. Additionally, the obligation is one-sided with no requirement for Valeant to share comparable data, creating an informational asymmetry disadvantageous to Dova.
findings.remediation: Limit to specific data categories (e.g., aggregated prescription data only), explicitly exclude competitively sensitive information (pricing, margins, strategic plans), require data reciprocity from Valeant, and narrowly define 'Valeant Activities' to exclude any activities relating to competing products.

findings.clause_text: Such information may include data from the applicable reimbursement HUB, specialty data aggregator, market research, and market access contracting and Third Party-provided brand performance data ([***])
findings.description: Obligation to share third party data without requiring consent, downstream confidentiality restrictions, or indemnification safeguards
findings.reasoning: Sharing 'Third Party-provided brand performance data' without ensuring Valeant is bound by the same restrictions Dova owes to third parties exposes Dova to breach of contract claims from data licensors. The clause lacks (1) representations that sharing complies with third party agreements, (2) flow-down confidentiality obligations, and (3) indemnification from Valeant for misuse or unauthorized further disclosure. This is particularly acute with reimbursement HUB data which may contain protected health information (PHI) and be subject to HIPAA and data use agreements.
findings.remediation: Add preconditions: (a) third party consent required before sharing, (b) Valeant must execute direct agreements with third parties where required, (c) explicit flow-down of confidentiality restrictions, (d) Valeant indemnification for third party claims arising from data misuse, and (e) exclusion of any data that cannot be shared without violating third party rights.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information... for use by Valeant and the Field Force Personnel in connection with the Valeant Activities
findings.description: Absence of data protection, security standards, use restrictions, and return/destruction obligations for shared data
findings.reasoning: The clause lacks essential data governance provisions: (1) no security standards (encryption, SOC 2) for transmission/storage, (2) no HIPAA business associate provisions despite likely PHI in reimbursement HUB data, (3) no prohibition on using data for purposes outside the co-promotion (e.g., Valeant's other products), (4) no return/destruction requirements upon termination, and (5) no audit rights. This creates regulatory liability (HIPAA, state privacy laws) and risk of permanent loss of control over proprietary data.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive data handling requirements: specific security standards, HIPAA BAA if applicable, explicit restriction on use for non-co-promotion purposes (including wall-off from Valeant's other business units), mandatory return/destruction of all data upon termination/expiration, audit rights, and certification of compliance.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information
findings.description: Absolute obligation to provide data without limitation of liability for accuracy, completeness, or reliance damages
findings.reasoning: Dova assumes unlimited liability for data accuracy without disclaimers. If Valeant relies on provided data for commercial decisions (e.g., resource allocation, targeting) and the data contains errors, Valeant could claim consequential damages for lost profits. The clause lacks 'AS IS' disclaimers and excludes the data sharing from general liability caps likely present elsewhere in the agreement.
findings.remediation: Add explicit disclaimer: data provided 'AS IS' without warranties of accuracy, completeness, or non-infringement; Valeant assumes all risk of reliance; expressly include data sharing within general liability cap; exclude consequential damages for data-related claims.

findings.clause_text: The timing of the delivery of such information shall be mutually agreed upon by the Parties, acting reasonably
findings.description: Vague 'mutual agreement' standard creates performance ambiguity and potential deadlock
findings.reasoning: While 'acting reasonably' appears protective, in practice this creates uncertainty about Dova's delivery obligations. Valeant could argue that Dova is unreasonably withholding agreement on timing or data scope, leading to disputes. Without objective standards or default timeframes, Dova lacks clear safe harbor for compliance.
findings.remediation: Replace with specific delivery schedules (e.g., monthly within 10 business days of month-end), objective criteria for 'reasonable' withholding (e.g., data unavailable, third party restrictions), and specify that mutual agreement is required only for modifications to standard reporting, not for basic performance.

findings.description: Absence of definitional scope for Valeant's permitted data use activities creates unlimited exposure for Dova's confidential, proprietary, and potentially protected health information
findings.reasoning: In pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements, the definition of permitted activities serves as the primary contractual boundary governing partner access to sensitive commercial data, prescriber information, patient data, and marketing strategies. Without this definitional limitation, Valeant could assert broad rights to use Dova data for purposes far beyond the co-promotion scope, including independent commercialization, competitive intelligence gathering, data aggregation for AI/machine learning training, or unauthorized sublicensing. This exposes Dova to potential HIPAA violations (if PHI is involved), trade secret misappropriation claims, loss of competitive advantage, and uncontrolled data proliferation that cannot be recalled post-termination.
findings.remediation: Insert comprehensive definition: 'Valeant Activities' means solely those specific sales, marketing, and promotional activities explicitly enumerated in Exhibit [X] and performed in strict compliance with Dova's written policies, standard operating procedures, and applicable laws. Valeant shall not use Dova Confidential Information (including any prescriber data, patient data, or commercial analytics) for any purpose other than performing Valeant Activities. Valeant is expressly prohibited from: (i) combining Dova data with third-party data sets; (ii) performing independent data analytics, benchmarking, or commercial exploitation; (iii) using Dova data to train AI/ML models; or (iv) sublicensing data access without prior written consent. All data use terminates immediately upon expiration or termination of this Agreement.'

findings.clause_ref: Confidentiality/NDA provisions (Article likely titled Confidentiality or similar)
findings.description: Confidentiality provisions text not provided or section is blank
findings.reasoning: In a pharmaceutical co-promotion agreement, confidentiality provisions are essential to protect trade secrets, proprietary manufacturing processes, regulatory filings, patient data, and marketing strategies. The absence of reviewed confidentiality language leaves Dova Pharmaceuticals exposed to unlimited liability for potential disclosure of Valeant's confidential information and unable to enforce protection of its own sensitive data. This gap prevents assessment of whether mutual obligations exist, whether exclusions for publicly available information are included, and whether survival periods post-termination are adequate.
findings.remediation: Immediately request the complete text of the Confidentiality/NDA article. Negotiate to include: (1) Mutual confidentiality obligations applicable to both parties; (2) Standard exclusions for information already public, independently developed, or rightfully received from third parties; (3) Permitted disclosures required by law or regulatory authorities with prior notice where possible; (4) Specific return or destruction procedures for confidential information upon termination; (5) Survival period of 3-5 years for general confidential information and perpetual survival for trade secrets; (6) Remedies clause acknowledging that monetary damages are insufficient for breach.

findings.clause_ref: HIPAA/Data Privacy Exhibit or Business Associate Agreement
findings.clause_text: [SECTION ABSENT - NO TEXT PROVIDED]
findings.description: Missing Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and data privacy exhibit in pharmaceutical co-promotion arrangement involving protected health information (PHI)
findings.reasoning: As outside counsel for Dova (product owner), the complete absence of a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement with Valeant (co-promotion partner) creates severe regulatory and liability exposure. Pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements inherently involve the exchange of patient health information (PHI), prescriber data, adverse event reports, and patient assistance program information. Without a compliant BAA, any disclosure of PHI to Valeant constitutes a per se violation of the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR 164.504(e)), exposing Dova to civil monetary penalties ranging from $137 to $68,928 per violation (up to $2.07 million annually for identical violations), potential criminal liability under 42 U.S.C. § 1320d-6, and reputational damage. Furthermore, the lack of contractual data security requirements means Valeant has no obligation to implement encryption, access controls, or audit trails, significantly increasing breach risk. Dova retains primary liability as the covered entity/pharmaceutical manufacturer while lacking contractual recourse against Valeant for downstream privacy breaches.
findings.remediation: Immediately negotiate and execute a comprehensive Business Associate Agreement (BAA) as a binding exhibit to the co-promotion agreement. The BAA must explicitly: (1) Define the specific, limited purposes for which Valeant may use PHI (restricted to co-promotion activities only) and prohibit any use beyond minimum necessary standards; (2) Require Valeant to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards compliant with 45 CFR §§ 164.308-164.312, including AES-256 encryption for data at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and annual penetration testing; (3) Establish strict breach notification timelines (not to exceed 24 hours upon discovery) and require Valeant to bear all costs of breach notification, credit monitoring, and regulatory fines; (4) Mandate that Valeant flow down BAA obligations to any subcontractors with access to PHI; (5) Require return or certified destruction of all PHI within 30 days of agreement termination; (6) Include Valeant's representation that it will not attempt to re-identify de-identified data or compile prescriber lists for competing products; (7) Add a mutual indemnification provision holding Valeant solely liable for breaches caused by its negligence or willful misconduct. Additionally, append a Data Security Exhibit addressing non-HIPAA protected data (e.g., GDPR, CCPA compliance) and establish Valeant as an independent contractor with no ownership rights in data generated during the co-promotion.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information relating to the sale, commercialization, marketing and promotion of the Product, as may be mutually agreed by the Parties from time to time
findings.description: Unfettered mandatory data sharing obligation without carve-outs for competitively sensitive, proprietary, or legally restricted data
findings.reasoning: The term 'shall' creates an absolute obligation without exceptions for data that may be competitively sensitive, subject to third-party confidentiality restrictions, protected as trade secrets, or where sharing would violate applicable law (including international data transfer restrictions). This exposes Dova to breach claims if it cannot share certain data due to pre-existing contractual or legal constraints, and forces Dova to choose between breaching this Agreement or third-party agreements.
findings.remediation: Amend to 'Dova shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide...' and add explicit carve-outs for information that (i) is competitively sensitive, (ii) is subject to third-party confidentiality obligations, (iii) constitutes proprietary trade secrets, (iv) is prohibited from disclosure by applicable law, or (v) would require disproportionate effort to extract. Add representation that Valeant acknowledges Dova may be limited by third-party agreements.

findings.clause_text: Third Party-provided brand performance data ([***])
findings.description: Obligation to share third-party data without requiring consent, indemnification, or verification of Dova's sharing rights
findings.reasoning: Dova likely has contractual restrictions with data providers (specialty pharmacies, market research firms) prohibiting or limiting sharing of this data. The clause does not require Dova to obtain third-party consent before sharing, nor does it require Valeant to indemnify Dova for claims arising from Valeant's use of such data. The redacted text prevents assessment of specific restrictions, creating unquantifiable exposure.
findings.remediation: Add requirement that Dova is only obligated to share third-party data to the extent (a) Dova has contractual rights to share, (b) any required consents are obtained at Valeant's cost, and (c) subject to the same confidentiality restrictions Dova is bound by. Add indemnification by Valeant for any claims arising from misuse or unauthorized sharing of third-party data by Valeant. Require disclosure of redacted restrictions before execution.

findings.clause_text: data from the applicable reimbursement HUB, specialty data aggregator
findings.description: Sharing of reimbursement HUB and specialty pharmacy data likely containing PHI without specified security standards or HIPAA Business Associate Agreement
findings.reasoning: Reimbursement HUBs and specialty data aggregators in pharmaceutical contexts routinely process patient identifiers, prescription information, and health data constituting Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA. The clause lacks (a) encryption requirements, (b) access controls, (c) audit trails, (d) breach notification procedures, and (e) most critically, a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA). Sharing PHI without a BAA violates 45 CFR Part 164, exposing Dova to civil penalties ($100-$50,000 per violation), criminal liability, and reputational damage.
findings.remediation: Immediately execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) compliant with 45 CFR Part 164 as an exhibit to this Agreement before any data exchange. Add technical safeguards: AES-256 encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, multi-factor authentication, and audit logging. Limit access to specific named Field Force Personnel with 'need to know' basis. Add breach notification within 24 hours and require Valeant to maintain cyber insurance with minimum $5M coverage. If no BAA can be executed, exclude PHI from data sharing obligations.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information relating to the sale, commercialization, marketing and promotion of the Product
findings.description: Absolute obligation to provide data without limitation of liability for accuracy, completeness, or reliance damages
findings.reasoning: Dova is required to provide data but the clause contains no limitation of liability for the accuracy or completeness of the data provided. If Valeant relies on inaccurate data to make commercial decisions and suffers losses, or if Dova inadvertently provides incomplete data, Dova faces unlimited liability for reliance damages, consequential damages, and lost profits. This is particularly dangerous given the 'shall' obligation which implies a warranty of performance.
findings.remediation: Add explicit disclaimer: 'All data is provided AS IS without warranty of accuracy, completeness, or fitness for purpose. Dova shall not be liable for any reliance damages, consequential damages, or lost profits arising from use of the data.' Cap liability for data-related claims at [specific amount] or limit to direct damages only. Add requirement that Valeant must independently verify all data before taking commercial action and expressly assumes risk of reliance.

findings.clause_text: as may be mutually agreed by the Parties from time to time
findings.description: Vague 'mutual agreement' standard creates performance ambiguity and potential deadlock without dispute resolution mechanism
findings.reasoning: The clause requires mutual agreement on the specific information to be shared, but provides no mechanism for resolving disputes if the parties cannot agree. 'Acting reasonably' (in the timing provision) is subjective and litigation-prone. If Valeant demands data Dova deems competitively sensitive, and they cannot agree, Dova faces potential breach claims for non-performance while Valeant claims Dova is not acting reasonably. This creates uncertainty and potential for tactical deadlock.
findings.remediation: Replace 'mutually agreed' with specific data specifications and delivery schedule in an exhibit. If flexibility is required, add tiered dispute resolution: (a) designated representatives negotiate for 10 days, (b) escalate to VP-level for 5 days, (c) if unresolved, Dova to provide data in accordance with industry standard practices for similar pharmaceutical products. Define 'acting reasonably' with objective criteria (e.g., response within 5 business days, providing data in standard formats).

findings.clause_text: for use by Valeant and the Field Force Personnel in connection with the Valeant Activities
findings.description: Broad use rights with undefined 'Valeant Activities' and no restrictions on secondary use, aggregation, or retention
findings.reasoning: 'Valeant Activities' is undefined in the provided text, potentially allowing unlimited use of Dova's confidential and proprietary data. The clause lacks restrictions on (a) combining Dova data with competitor products or data, (b) using data for purposes outside the specific co-promotion, (c) sublicensing to other third parties, (d) creating derivative databases, or (e) retaining data after termination. This destroys data exclusivity, creates competitive harm risks, and violates data minimization principles.
findings.remediation: Define 'Valeant Activities' narrowly as 'the specific co-promotion activities for the Product expressly authorized in Section [X] and limited to the Territory.' Add explicit prohibitions on: (a) use for any product other than the Product, (b) disclosure to any party other than specific named Field Force Personnel, (c) creation of derivative databases combining with other data sources without consent, (d) use for competitive analysis against Dova, and (e) retention beyond the Agreement term. Add audit rights for Dova to verify compliance.

findings.clause_text: Dova shall provide to Valeant certain information relating to the sale, commercialization, marketing and promotion of the Product
findings.description: Missing data return, destruction, and certification obligations upon termination or expiration
findings.reasoning: While the clause creates an obligation to share data, it is silent on post-termination obligations. Without explicit return or destruction requirements, Valeant could retain and continue to exploit Dova's confidential commercial data and any PHI indefinitely after the co-promotion relationship ends. This violates data privacy principles, HIPAA requirements for PHI disposal, and creates ongoing competitive harm risks. The absence of a certification requirement makes enforcement impossible.
findings.remediation: Add provision requiring Valeant within 30 days of termination/expiration to: (a) return all Dova data in its original format or as directed by Dova, or (b) securely destroy all copies (electronic and physical) using NIST 800-88 standards and provide written certification of destruction signed by a senior officer. For any PHI, require destruction in accordance with the BAA and HIPAA. Specify that Field Force Personnel must certify compliance and that Dova has audit rights to verify destruction.

findings.clause_text: neither Dova nor is Affiliates shall, directly or indirectly, [***]
findings.description: Grammatical error creating ambiguity regarding Affiliate coverage scope
findings.reasoning: The text states 'nor is Affiliates' rather than 'nor its Affiliates.' This typographical error creates contractual ambiguity as to whether Dova's Affiliates are bound by the non-compete obligations. Judges may apply the principle of contra proferentem against the drafter (likely Valeant), potentially excusing Dova's Affiliates from compliance, or Valeant may argue it excuses their Affiliates by parity of construction. This undermines the exclusivity protections Dova requires.
findings.remediation: Immediate correction to 'nor its Affiliates' with explicit confirmation that the provision applies to all Affiliates as defined in Section [X]. Consider adding 'and its and their respective successors and assigns' to ensure coverage post-acquisition.

findings.clause_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section 2.3.1(a) shall not apply to any products marketed, promoted, detailed, offered for sale, or sold by any business (or any portion thereof), other Person, or group of Persons, [***]
findings.description: Overly broad acquisition carve-out eviscerates non-compete protection
findings.reasoning: The carve-out exempts products marketed by 'any business (or any portion thereof)' that is acquired or associated with the parties. This allows Valeant (which has a history of aggressive acquisitions) to acquire a direct competitor of the Product and continue commercializing it, effectively gutting Dova's exclusivity. The phrase 'any portion thereof' permits Valeant to claim competing products are merely a 'portion' of a larger acquired business to avoid restrictions.
findings.remediation: Narrow the exception to: (i) exclude products acquired after the Effective Date that compete with the Product; or (ii) require divestiture or cessation of promotion within 90-180 days post-acquisition; and (iii) add anti-circumvention language: 'provided that no party shall acquire any business for the purpose of circumventing this Section 2.3.1.'

findings.clause_text: provided that if the Agreement is terminated by Dova pursuant to [***], then any Tail Period shall be immediately terminated if either Valeant or any of its Affiliates, directly or indirectly, [***] in the Territory other than the Product during such Tail Period
findings.description: Asymmetrical Tail Period termination mechanism creating unilateral escape risk
findings.reasoning: This provision allows Valeant to unilaterally terminate its Tail Period (and associated obligations/payments) simply by commencing competition. While this provides Dova a remedy to stop Tail payments, it also gives Valeant a 'put option' to exit transition obligations prematurely. More critically, Section 2.3.1(b) lacks visible reciprocal language ensuring Dova can similarly terminate obligations if Valeant competes, or confirming Dova's Tail Period continues regardless. This asymmetry may force Dova to continue providing transition services while Valeant competes freely.
findings.remediation: Ensure Section 2.3.1(b) contains identical reciprocal termination rights. Alternatively, amend to state that 'Dova may, at its sole election, terminate the Tail Period immediately upon written notice' rather than automatic termination, preventing Valeant from forcing premature exit.

findings.remediation: Verify the redacted language includes comprehensive restrictions: 'research, develop, manufacture, commercialize, promote, market, detail, distribute, sell, offer for sale, import, export, or directly or indirectly invest in (including through debt or equity), consult for, or provide services regarding any product competitive with the Product.'

findings.clause_text: 2.3.1 Non-Competition
findings.description: Missing standard exceptions for passive investments and pre-existing products
findings.reasoning: Standard pharmaceutical co-promotion non-competes typically exclude: (a) passive investments of less than 5% in publicly traded entities, and (b) products in a party's pipeline as of the Effective Date. The absence of these exceptions, combined with the broad 'business' carve-out, creates uncertainty. Valeant may argue its existing products are exempt under the carve-out, while Dova remains over-restricted from normal investment activities.
findings.remediation: Add explicit exceptions: (i) ownership of less than [5]% of publicly traded securities; (ii) products being developed or commercialized by a party as of the Effective Date, provided such products are listed on Schedule [X]; and (iii) internal basic research activities not directed toward commercialization.

findings.clause_text: [Content Not Provided - Reference Only: Section 12.6 (referenced in cross-references) to determine full Tail Period mechanics]
findings.description: Missing Tail Period mechanics clause prevents assessment of post-termination payment obligations, data rights, and wind-down liabilities
findings.reasoning: Section 12.6 contains critical Tail Period provisions governing financial obligations following termination of the co-promotion agreement. Without visibility into these mechanics, Dova cannot assess: (1) the duration of the Tail Period and associated payment obligations to Valeant (potentially ranging from 6 months to several years); (2) whether payments during the Tail Period are based on net sales, gross sales, or other metrics; (3) data access, reporting, and audit rights Valeant retains post-termination; (4) ownership and usage rights of promotional materials, customer lists, and medical education content developed during the term; (5) wind-down obligations and transition assistance requirements; and (6) liability limitations (or lack thereof) for activities conducted during the Tail Period. This creates unquantified financial exposure potentially worth millions in ongoing royalty-like payments and operational risk regarding data handling and IP ownership. Given Valeant's (now Bausch Health) historical negotiating posture favoring aggressive post-termination rights, the absence of this section is particularly concerning.
findings.remediation: Immediately request full text of Section 12.6 before proceeding with agreement execution. Negotiate for: (1) Tail Period duration capped at 6-12 months maximum (not rolling or indefinite); (2) Declining payment scale during Tail Period (e.g., 100% months 1-6, 50% months 7-12); (3) Explicit exclusion of Tail Period payments for sales to new customers acquired post-termination; (4) Clear data destruction or return obligations within 30-60 days of Tail Period end; (5) Explicit IP ownership retention by Dova with limited license to Valeant only during active Tail Period; (6) Cap on liability for post-termination activities; and (7) Right for Dova to terminate Tail Period early with payment of predetermined buyout amount.

findings.clause_ref: Definition of 'Tail Period' to confirm duration and payment obligations
findings.description: Missing definition of 'Tail Period' creates unlimited post-termination payment obligations and operational uncertainty for Dova
findings.reasoning: In co-promotion agreements, the Tail Period governs the duration of trailing commissions owed to Valeant following termination and controls wind-down activities. Without a defined Tail Period, Valeant could assert rights to indefinite commissions on prescriptions influenced during the term but filled post-termination, exposing Dova to uncapped financial liability that could continue for years. The absence of defined duration limits (standard: 6-12 months), payment caps, activity restrictions, and data handling protocols prevents Dova from budgeting termination costs, controlling customer transition, or preventing Valeant from leveraging Dova's confidential information for competing products during an undefined wind-down period.
findings.remediation: Negotiate insertion of a comprehensive Tail Period definition including: (1) explicit duration limitation (6-12 months maximum post-termination); (2) aggregate cap on total commissions payable during Tail Period; (3) restriction of commissions to prescriptions written by specific physicians detailed by Valeant during a defined look-back period (e.g., last 6 months of term); (4) prohibition on Valeant conducting any active promotional activities during Tail Period (passive commission receipt only); (5) mandatory data return and destruction obligations; (6) verification mechanics to prevent duplicate payments; and (7) clarification that no minimum guarantees apply during Tail Period.

findings.description: Section 2.3.1(b) is completely missing from the contract text provided for verification. This creates a critical documentation gap where termination rights cannot be confirmed as reciprocal.
findings.reasoning: The original analysis flagged a coverage gap regarding reciprocal termination rights in Section 2.3. The current request asks to verify Section 2.3.1(b) specifically, but no text has been provided. Without the actual clause text, we cannot confirm whether Dova has equivalent termination rights to Valeant, whether notice periods are balanced, whether termination fees or wind-down obligations are symmetrical, or whether post-termination transition assistance obligations apply equally. This missing section is particularly critical in a co-promotion agreement where termination asymmetries could leave Dova locked into an unfavorable arrangement while Valeant retains easy exit rights, or vice versa. The cross-reference from Section 12.6 to Section 2.3 suggests termination provisions are interconnected, making this gap even more significant.
findings.remediation: Immediately obtain the complete text of Section 2.3.1(b) and all related subsections (2.3.1(a), 2.3.2, etc.). Negotiate to ensure: (1) both parties have equivalent termination triggers and notice periods; (2) any termination fees or wind-down costs are allocated proportionally or equally; (3) post-termination transition assistance (data transfer, regulatory filings, customer handoff) applies symmetrically; (4) survival clauses for confidentiality, IP, and indemnification are identical regardless of which party terminates; and (5) no party has 'for convenience' termination rights without equivalent compensation or cure periods.

findings.clause_text: provided that if the Agreement is terminated by Dova pursuant to [***], then any Tail Period shall be immediately terminated if either Valeant or any of its Affiliates, directly or indirectly, [***] in the Territory other than the Product during such Tail Period
findings.description: Asymmetrical Tail Period termination mechanism creating unilateral escape risk
findings.reasoning: The clause creates a mechanism where Dova can immediately terminate the Tail Period (which likely contains post-termination payment obligations, data rights, or wind-down benefits) if Valeant competes during such period. However, there is no corresponding provision in Section 2.3.1(b) allowing Valeant to terminate Dova's Tail Period if Dova competes. This creates a one-sided risk exposure where Valeant's post-termination benefits are conditional and forfeitable, while Dova's obligations (if any Tail Period exists for Dova) appear unconditional. Additionally, the termination trigger is redacted ([***]), preventing assessment of whether this applies to termination for convenience or only for cause.
findings.remediation: Negotiate reciprocal Tail Period termination rights for both parties, ensuring that either party can terminate the other's Tail Period upon competition. Alternatively, remove the termination mechanism entirely to ensure Tail Period obligations remain unconditional. Disclose the redacted termination triggers to ensure they are limited to termination for material breach.

findings.clause_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section 2.3.1(a) shall not apply to any products marketed, promoted, detailed, offered for sale, or sold by any business (or any portion thereof), other Person, or group of Persons, [***]
findings.description: Overly broad acquisition carve-out eviscerates non-compete protection
findings.reasoning: The carve-out exempts from the non-compete any products from 'any business (or any portion thereof), other Person, or group of Persons.' This language is extraordinarily broad and effectively nullifies the non-compete. Valeant could acquire a direct competitor, a division of a competitor, or a group of Persons engaged in competing activities, and immediately market competing products without violating the non-compete. The phrase 'any portion thereof' is particularly problematic as it suggests acquiring even a small division or product line of a competitor triggers the exemption. The redacted text at the end ([***]) may contain limitations, but as written, the carve-out is unlimited.
findings.remediation: Narrow the carve-out to apply only to: (a) products existing prior to the acquisition date that were actively marketed by the acquired entity prior to acquisition; (b) acquisitions where the competing products represent less than a specified percentage (e.g., 20%) of the acquired entity's revenue; (c) require that the acquired entity was not acquired primarily to circumvent the non-compete; and (d) add a revenue threshold for the acquired business (e.g., only applies to businesses with revenue exceeding $X million).

findings.clause_text: "Third Party Agreements" shall mean the agreements described on Schedule 1.65 hereto.
findings.description: Uncritical incorporation by reference of unreviewed Schedule 1.65 creates material uncertainty regarding scope of third-party obligations, exclusivity restrictions, and potential royalty stacking liabilities
findings.reasoning: The definition incorporates Schedule 1.65 without (i) appending the schedule for diligence review, (ii) limiting the scope to Material Agreements (by dollar threshold or strategic significance), (iii) qualifying by execution date (existing vs. future), or (iv) specifying whether summaries or full agreements are disclosed. In a pharmaceutical co-promotion context, Third Party Agreements typically include license agreements, supply contracts, distribution arrangements, or government pricing agreements that may contain: (a) exclusivity or non-compete provisions restricting Valeant's activities in the co-promotion territory; (b) change-of-control or assignment clauses requiring consent for the co-promotion structure; (c) royalty pass-through or milestone payment obligations that affect profitability; or (d) sublicense restrictions limiting Dova's ability to authorize Valeant's promotion activities. Without prior review, Dova assumes unquantified risk of hidden restrictions that could impede the co-promotion or trigger breach-of-contract claims from third parties. Additionally, if Valeant retains unilateral rights to amend Schedule 1.65 post-execution, Dova would be bound to future undisclosed obligations.
findings.remediation: 1) Conditionally define term upon attachment of complete Schedule 1.65 with full copies (not summaries) of all agreements; 2) Amend definition to 'Material Third Party Agreements' exceeding $[X] in annual payments or containing exclusivity/IP/territory restrictions; 3) Add temporal qualifier limiting to agreements 'in effect as of the Effective Date' and requiring mutual written consent for any post-signing additions; 4) Include representation in Section 10 that no Third Party Agreement contains exclusivity conflicting with the co-promotion territory, requires consent for the transaction, or imposes undisclosed payment obligations; 5) Require Valeant to indemnify Dova for losses arising from undisclosed Third Party Agreement restrictions.

findings.clause_text: [SCHEDULE NOT PROVIDED/ATTACHED - Content missing]

Immediately obtain and attach the complete Schedule 1.65 listing all Third Party Agreements with material terms (counterparty, effective date, territory, field of use, exclusivity status, sublicense rights, termination provisions). 2. If no such agreements exist, explicitly state 'Schedule 1.65 is intentionally left blank' or 'As of the Effective Date, there are no Third Party Agreements.' 3. Add a representation and warranty from Dova that Schedule 1.65 contains all material agreements affecting the product rights and that no undisclosed agreements restrict the rights granted to Valeant. 4. findings.clause_text: "Third Party Agreements" (defined in 1.65): shall mean the agreements described on Schedule 1.65 hereto.
findings.description: The defined term creates contractual ambiguity by referencing a missing schedule, preventing assessment of third-party encumbrances on co-promotion rights.
findings.reasoning: In pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements, Third Party Agreements typically include: (1) in-licensing agreements from universities or biotechs that may restrict sublicensing without consent, (2) manufacturing agreements with sole-source suppliers, (3) distribution agreements with exclusive territories that may conflict with co-promotion territories, and (4) development agreements with data sharing restrictions. The definition incorporates these agreements by reference to Schedule 1.65, making them part of the contract. However, since the schedule is missing, Valeant cannot perform due diligence on: whether sublicensing rights exist (critical for co-promotion), whether exclusivity is maintained (critical for Valeant's investment), whether manufacturing supply is assured (critical for commercialization), and whether there are change-of-control provisions that could terminate underlying rights upon execution of this agreement. This creates unmitigated business and legal risk.
findings.remediation: 1. Require Dova to provide a complete list of all Third Party Agreements with summaries of material terms including: licensor name, licensed IP, territory, field, exclusivity (yes/no), sublicense rights (yes/no with/without consent), termination for change of control (yes/no), and any restrictions on co-promotion or detailing activities. 2. Add a representation that Dova has provided all material Third Party Agreements and that no other agreements restrict the rights granted to Valeant under this Agreement. 3. Include specific indemnification for breach of this representation with a minimum cap appropriate to the value of the co-promotion rights. 4. Add a covenant that Dova will maintain all Third Party Agreements in full force and effect, not amend or terminate them without Valeant's consent (if they affect Valeant's rights), and provide annual certifications of compliance. 5. Obtain legal opinions regarding the validity and enforceability of key Third Party Agreements.

findings.clause_text: Cross-reference: 10.1.13 -> 1.65 (as_defined_in)
findings.description: Cross-reference to undefined schedule creates compliance monitoring and covenant performance risks regarding ongoing obligations tied to Third Party Agreements.
findings.reasoning: The cross-reference from Section 10.1.13 to the definition in 1.65 (which incorporates Schedule 1.65) suggests that Section 10.1 likely contains covenants, compliance obligations, or termination rights related to Third Party Agreements. Common provisions in co-promotion agreements at Section 10.1 might include: obligations to maintain third-party licenses in force, requirements to obtain third-party consents for certain activities, termination rights if third-party agreements are breached, or compliance with third-party audit rights. Without knowing what Third Party Agreements exist (Schedule 1.65 missing) and without seeing Section 10.1.13 text, Valeant cannot: (1) monitor compliance with covenants that may depend on Third Party Agreement terms, (2) assess whether Dova's maintenance of Third Party Agreements is satisfactory, (3) determine if Valeant has any obligations to assist with Third Party Agreement compliance, or (4) evaluate termination risks if Third Party Agreements are terminated. This creates operational uncertainty and potential breach risks.
findings.remediation: 1. Obtain the full text of Section 10.1.13 to understand the specific obligations referencing Third Party Agreements. 2. Negotiate for a covenant that Dova will: (i) maintain all Third Party Agreements in full force and effect, (ii) not amend or terminate them without Valeant's prior written consent (to the extent they affect Valeant's rights), (iii) promptly cure any defaults, and (iv) provide annual certifications of compliance. 3. Add a right for Valeant to receive immediate notice (within 5 business days) of any defaults, termination threats, or amendments to Third Party Agreements. 4. Include a termination right for Valeant if material Third Party Agreements are terminated or amended in a way that materially adversely affects Valeant's rights. 5. Ensure Valeant has audit rights to verify compliance with Third Party Agreements.

findings.clause_text: [Empty section - cross-reference usage of Third Party Agreements as defined in Section 1.65]
findings.description: Cross-reference to Third Party Agreements creates undefined compliance obligations and unlimited liability exposure without liability caps, indemnification limitations, or responsibility allocations between the parties.
findings.reasoning: Section 10.1.13 incorporates Third Party Agreements (defined in Section 1.65 and listed on Schedule 1.65) by reference without specifying: (a) which party bears responsibility for compliance with these third-party agreements; (b) liability limitations for breaches of such agreements; or (c) indemnification obligations arising thereunder. As outside counsel for Dova (product owner), this exposes Dova to potential liability for breaches of Valeant's (co-promotion partner) third-party agreements, or for uncapped obligations under third-party agreements that may relate to the co-promotion activities. The lack of liability caps or mutual indemnification provisions regarding Third Party Agreements violates standard risk allocation principles in pharmaceutical co-promotion agreements.
findings.remediation: Amend Section 10.1.13 to explicitly state that: (1) each party is solely responsible for compliance with its own Third Party Agreements; (2) neither party shall be liable for the other party's breach of, or claims arising under, the other party's Third Party Agreements; (3) Dova shall not be required to indemnify Valeant for any claims arising from Valeant's Third Party Agreements, and vice versa; and (4) any liability related to Third Party Agreements shall be subject to the aggregate liability caps set forth in Section [X] of the Agreement. Alternatively, if the cross-reference serves no substantive purpose, delete Section 10.1.13 entirely.
